Naha 103

Kokusai-dōri · Makishi Public Market · Tsuboya · Shuri Castle · Naminoue · Sakaemachi

  1. Must see · Naha

    Shikinaen Royal Garden (識名園)

    The Ryūkyū royal family’s largest villa garden, built around a pond with jagged coral-limestone bridges two kilometres south of Shuri Castle; used to receive Chinese envoys and now a UNESCO component.

    Look for Royal villa garden

    421-7 Maaji, Naha, Okinawa 902-0072, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Japan-guide, Visit Okinawa, Lonely Planet

  2. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Naha

    Urizun (古酒と琉球料理 うりずん)

    Opened 15 August 1972 by gathering bottles from every awamori distillery in Okinawa — the bar that brought awamori back to the people. Order duru-ten, the fried taro croquette Okinawa Times traces to this kitchen, and a flight of kūsu (aged awamori).

    388-5 Asato, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Prefecture — 「琉球料理が味わえる店」 certification, Okinawa Times, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  3. Must see · Naha

    Tamaudun Royal Mausoleum (玉陵)

    Limestone tomb of the second Shō dynasty, built in 1501 under King Shō Shin and modelled on Shuri Castle, its balustrades carved with dragons, phoenixes and lions. A National Treasure as well as a UNESCO component.

    Look for Royal tomb, National Treasure

    1-3 Kinjo-cho, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Japan-guide, Visit Okinawa

  4. Must see · Naha

    Tsuboya Yachimun-dōri pottery street (壺屋やちむん通り)

    The Ryūkyū Kingdom's ceramics quarter: a 400 m stone-paved street between Kokusai-dōri and Route 330 lined with potteries, kilns and shops selling yachimun ware and shisa, with wheel-throwing classes.

    Look for Historic pottery street

    Tsuboya, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa, Japan-guide

  5. Must see · Naha

    Kokusai-dōri (国際通り)

    Naha's 1.6 km main street of shops, cafés, bars and awamori stores, rebuilt so fast after 1945 it was nicknamed the 'Miracle Mile'; the gateway to Makishi market, Tsuboya and the arcades, and the stage for the city's big festivals.

    Look for Main street

    Kumoji–Makishi–Matsuo, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Japan-guide

  6. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Shuri Soba (首里そば)

    Lunch-only Shuri shop carrying on the noodle technique of a vanished Shuri original: unbleached flour pressed and rested over two days, a single soba on the menu, queues from before opening and sold out early.

    Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawa Times

  7. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Mendokoro Tiandaa (麺処 てぃあんだー)

    Cult Naha soba shop known for house-made noodles; the fūchibā soba arrives fragrant with Okinawan mugwort. In both Okinawa Traveler's soba feature and Mapple's Okinawa-soba round-up.

    Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawatraveler, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  8. Must see · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Naha

    Karakara to Chibugwā (カラカラとちぶぐゎ〜)

    Naha's awamori-specialist bar: bottles from every distillery in the prefecture and aged kūsu past thirty years, with three awamori sommeliers to steer you; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine.

    Yamako 2nd Bldg 1F, 3-15-15 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawatraveler, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawa Prefecture — 「琉球料理が味わえる店」 certification

  9. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Naha

    Kozakura (小桜)

    A seventy-year-old koryōriya off Kokusai-dōri, believed to be the oldest surviving restaurant of its era in Naha; the third-generation owner keeps both old and new Okinawan dishes on the menu.

    3-12-21 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  10. Must see · Teishoku, Curry & Yōshoku · Naha

    Keishoku no Mise Ruby, Tomari (軽食の店ルビー)

    Sixty-plus-year-old Tomari diner whose name belies mountainous portions: some 80 dishes from champuru to loco moco, but half the room orders the C-lunch. Namie Amuro used to drop in after dance practice.

    Tomari, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Okinawatraveler, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  11. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Naha

    Fujiya Tomari Honten (富士家 泊本店)

    The name many Okinawans give first for zenzai: fluffy shaved ice frozen from the bean-cooking syrup so it never dilutes, heaped over sweet kintoki beans. Open daily, later hours in summer.

    2-10-9 Tomari, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Hismag, Tabirai

  12. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Naha

    Kokusai-dōri Yatai-mura (国際通り屋台村)

    A food-stall village opened in 2015 just off Kokusai-dōri, with more than 20 counter stalls cooking Okinawan and island dishes from local ingredients — gurukun and parrotfish sushi, Agu pork dumplings, Ishigaki beef — from 11:00. A central stage hosts island songs and dances.

    Kokusai-dōri, Makishi, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Okinawatraveler, Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Fun! Japan (JTB)

  13. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Okinawa Daiichi Hotel breakfast (沖縄第一ホテル 薬膳朝食)

    A five-room hotel founded in 1955 whose medicinal-herb breakfast, devised by founder Shimabukuro Yoshiko from her mother's recipes about 40 years ago, uses some 50 ingredients across 20+ Okinawan dishes (about ¥3,300). One of Naha's famous breakfasts; reservation advised.

    1-1-12 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by All About (allabout.co.jp), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  14. Must see · Naha

    Shuri Castle (首里城)

    Palace of the Ryūkyū Kingdom from 1429 to 1879 and the centrepiece of the UNESCO Gusuku Sites. Destroyed in 1945 and again by fire in 2019; the rebuilt Seiden (main hall) exterior is complete, its interior due to reopen on 23 November 2026.

    Look for UNESCO World Heritage gusuku; Seiden rebuild

    1-2 Kinjo-cho, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Japan-guide

  15. Must see · Naha

    Makishi Public Market (第一牧志公設市場)

    Naha’s kitchen since 1950: 75 ground-floor stalls of spiny lobster, reef fish, pork and island produce, with upstairs restaurants that cook what you buy (mochiage). Reopened in a new building on 19 March 2023.

    Look for Post-war market, rebuilt 2023

    2-10-1 Matsuo, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Govonline

  16. Must see · Naha

    Kinjō-chō Ishidatami-michi stone-paved road (金城町石畳道)

    About 300 m survive of the c.1522 limestone-paved royal road that ran south from Shuri Castle, winding steeply between old stone walls and red-tiled houses.

    Look for Ryūkyū-era cobbled lane

    Kinjo-cho, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  17. Must see · Naha

    Okinawa Prefectural Museum & Art Museum (沖縄県立博物館・美術館)

    The prefecture's flagship museum in Shintoshin: Ryūkyū history, nature and crafts from prehistory to the US era, with a modern Okinawan art wing.

    Look for History & art museum

    3-1-1 Omoromachi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  18. Must see · Wagyu, Yakiniku & Sukiyaki · Naha

    Jack's Steak House (ジャッキーステーキハウス)

    Opened in 1953 under the US occupation and still displaying its 'A-sign' — the US-military approval certificate; the benchmark of Okinawa's post-war steak culture, open till 1 a.m.

    1-7-3 Nishi, Naha, Okinawa 900-0036, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Savor Japan

  19. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Yūnangi (ゆうなんぎい)

    Family-run Okinawan restaurant on a side street off Kokusai-dōri, serving home cooking since 1970 under US administration — hard to get a seat, rated among the best Okinawan food in Naha.

    3-3-3 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  20. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Ryūkyū Cuisine Mie (琉球料理 美榮)

    Founded in 1958 to reproduce the Ryūkyū royal court cuisine of Shō Junnan, gourmet son of the last king, in a wooden two-storey ryōtei behind a formal gate in Kumoji.

    Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by The Japan Times, Bunka Survey

  21. Must see · Kissaten & Coffee · Naha

    Tamagusuku Coffee Roasters (タマグスクコーヒー)

    Ten-seat roaster-café off Kokusai-dōri often called the island's best cup: the owner asks what you like, then drips light-to-dark single origins one cup at a time.

    2-19-39 Matsuo, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan Travel (japantravel.com), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  22. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Naha

    Benriya Yulinglong, Sakaemachi (べんり屋 玉玲瓏)

    The pioneer of Sakaemachi market's night drinking: when the stalls shutter, tables fill the alley for its hand-made gyōza. Both Rurubu and Mapple name it first among the market's after-dark haunts.

    388-1 Asato, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  23. Must see · Markets, Depachika & Street Food · Naha

    Tomari Iyumachi Fish Market (泊いゆまち)

    The Okinawa fisheries co-op's market by Tomari Port, where about 70 percent of the catch sold is tuna, delivered unfrozen the day it is landed. Stalls sell sashimi, seafood bowls, shellfish and mozuku to eat on the upstairs terrace.

    1-1-18 Minatomachi, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Naha City (official municipal publications)

  24. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Naha

    Ryūkyū Ryōri Nuchigafū (琉球料理 ぬちがふぅ)

    An elegant hilltop restaurant above the southern end of Tsuboya pottery street that Lonely Planet singles out for a memorable dinner of Ryūkyū cuisine. It is on Okinawa Prefecture's certified list of restaurants serving authentic Ryūkyū cuisine.

    Tsuboya, Naha, Okinawa (hilltop off the southern end of Tsuboya Yachimun-dōri)

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Okinawa Prefecture — 「琉球料理が味わえる店」 certification

  25. Worth the detour · Naha

    Shuri Ryusen bingata & coral-dye studio (首里琉染)

    Bingata workshop and shop five minutes' walk from Shuri Castle Park, selling bingata and its own 'coral-dye' (sango-zome) textiles. Upstairs visitors can try coral dyeing (about 50 minutes) and watch artisans dyeing in the third-floor studio.

    Look for Try Ryūkyū coral-dyeing beside Shuri Castle

    1-54 Shuri Yamagawa-chō, Naha, Okinawa 903-0825, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Ocvb, Nahanavi, Okinawatraveler

  26. Worth the detour · Naha

    Kume Shiseibyō Confucius Temple (久米至聖廟)

    Naha's Confucian temple, a centre of Chinese learning for the Ryūkyū Kingdom since the original was built in 1671–75; its precinct holds the Meirindō, Okinawa's first public school. Rebuilt in Kume in 2013 beside Fukushū-en, on the old Chinese-émigré Kume village.

    Look for The Ryūkyū Kingdom's Confucian temple, in old Kume village

    2-30-1 Kume, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wiki, Wikipedia JA, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Japan Experience

  27. Worth the detour · Naha

    Bin-nu-utaki / Bengadake Sacred Grove (弁之御嶽・弁ヶ嶽)

    At 165.7 m the highest point in Naha, about 1 km east of Shuri Castle. In the Ryūkyū Kingdom it was a state place of worship where the king, or his envoy, prayed for his health and the nation's peace; designated a National Historic Site as 'Bin-nu-utaki' on 15 October 2018.

    Look for Naha's highest hill, a royal prayer site behind Shuri

    Shuri Torihori-chō, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Agency For Cultural Affairs, Ocvb, Wikipedia JA, Tabirai

  28. Worth the detour · Naha

    Asato Hachimangū Shrine (安里八幡宮)

    One of the Ryūkyū Hassha, founded in the Tianshun era (1457–64) and enshrining Emperor Ōjin, Empress Jingū and Tamayori-hime; the only Hachiman shrine among the eight. A short walk from Asato and Omoromachi stations.

    Look for The Ryūkyū Eight's 15th-century Hachiman shrine

    124 Asato, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Kotobank, Jinjacho, Official Site

  29. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Ryōtei Naha, Tsuji (料亭那覇)

    A ryōtei founded in 1949 in Tsuji, Naha's old entertainment quarter, now over 70 years old. Dinner is a set Ryūkyū or Japanese-Ryūkyū course served while professional dancers perform classical Ryūkyū dance. It holds the 'Ryūkyū ryōri ga ajiwaeru mise' certification and is listed by OCVB and Rurubu.

    2-2-11 Tsuji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyuryori, Ocvb, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Nahanavi

  30. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Yaeyama Ryōri Kotōzan Tantei, Shuri (八重山料理 虎頭山 潭亭)

    A reservation-only Yaeyama-cuisine restaurant on Torazuyama hill in Shuri, looking out over Naha and Shuri Castle. Most ingredients come from Ishigaki, and the owner does every step of the cooking. It is a certified Ryūkyū-cuisine shop and is profiled by OCVB, Tabirai and Okinawa Traveler.

    2-40-1 Shuri Akahira-chō, Naha, Okinawa 903-0811, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyuryori, Ocvb, Tabirai, Okinawatraveler

  31. Worth the detour · Ramen & Tsukemen · Naha

    Ryūkyū Shinmen Tondō, Oroku Honten (琉球新麺 通堂 小禄本店)

    The flagship of Okinawa's best-known ramen brand, billed as the world's first 'ramen with a gender': a thick, smooth tonkotsu 'men's taste' and a clear salt-chicken 'women's taste'. Open straight through from 11:00 to late night and packed with locals and visitors. The brand was also selected as a guest shop at the Shin-Yokohama Rāmen Museum.

    5-4-6 Kanagusuku, Naha, Okinawa 〒901-0155

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), TVBS Supertaste (食尚玩家), Marie Claire Taiwan, Shin-Yokohama Raumen Museum

  32. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Naha

    BAR Owl, Kumoji (バー オウル)

    Cocktail bar in Naha's Kumoji business district behind a heavy door, with a counter lined with tropical fruit; known for showy seasonal-fruit cocktails such as Okinawan mikan, and awamori cocktails. Selected for Tabelog's Bar 100 (2022).

    Kanetomo Sangyō Bldg 2F, 1-8-7 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa 〒900-0015

    Recommended by Culture Trip, Fun! Japan (JTB), Tabelog Hyakumeiten, Ocvb

  33. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Naha

    Kōhī Sakan Inshallah, Kokusai-dōri (珈琲茶館インシャラー)

    Coffee house on Kokusai-dōri trading since 1974, themed on Arabia as coffee's birthplace and serving Turkish and Arabic coffees. Its signature 'Paris no Romance' has rose cream swirling in the cup as the coffee is poured at the table.

    1-3-63 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Feeljapan, Retrip (rtrp.jp) travel magazine, Kokusaidori, Official Site

  34. Worth the detour · Naha

    Tomari International Cemetery (泊外人墓地)

    A small walled cemetery on the north bank of Tomari Port holding about 22 foreigners from the 18th to early 20th centuries and some 300 post-war burials, with a monument to Commodore Perry's 1853 landing. Its oldest Western grave, of the British sailor 'WM HARES', is dated 1816.

    Look for Historic foreigners' cemetery & Perry landing monument

    Tomari, Naha, Okinawa (north shore of Tomari Port)

    Recommended by SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives), Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  35. Worth the detour · Naha

    Arakaki Family Residence, Tsuboya (新垣家住宅)

    The only surviving 18th-century Tsuboya potter's compound — red-tiled main house, workshop, climbing kiln (the former royal 'Higashi-nu-kama') and stone pigsty-toilet — designated an Important Cultural Property in 2002.

    Look for Important Cultural Property · Tsuboya potter's house & climbing kiln

    1-28-32 Tsuboya, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Agency For Cultural Affairs, Tabimag, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報)

  36. Worth the detour · Naha

    Tsushima Maru Memorial Museum (対馬丸記念館)

    Museum (opened 22 Aug 2004) on the 1944 sinking of the evacuation ship Tsushima Maru, in which hundreds of Okinawan schoolchildren died; run by the Tsushima Maru Memorial Association beside Gokoku-ji and Naminoue.

    Look for WWII memorial museum · 1944 child-evacuee ship

    1-25 Wakasa, Naha, Okinawa 〒900-0031

    Recommended by Wiki, Official Site, Internet Museum (museum.or.jp)

  37. Worth the detour · Naha

    Heiwa-dōri Shopping Arcade (平和通り商店街)

    Covered arcade of around 200 shops branching off Kokusai-dōri toward Makishi Public Market, nicknamed the 'labyrinth arcade'. Named 'Peace Street' by public competition in 1951 after the Heiwa-kan cinema at its mouth; a new generation of shop owners has revived it since the 2000s.

    Look for Naha's roofed 'labyrinth arcade' off Kokusai-dōri

    3-3 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wiki, Ocvb, Tabimag

  38. Worth the detour · Naha

    Yogi Park cherry blossoms (与儀公園)

    City park that is Naha's best-known cherry-blossom spot, with more than 400 Kanhizakura (Taiwan cherry) trees. They flower among Japan's earliest, and the Naha Cherry Blossom Festival is held here in early February.

    Look for Naha's February cherry-blossom park

    1-1 Yogi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Ocvb, Matcha — Japan travel web magazine

  39. Worth the detour · Naha

    Shikina-gū Shrine (識名宮)

    One of the Ryūkyū Hassha, the eight shrines given royal patronage by the Ryūkyū Kingdom, near Shikinaen in Hantagawa. Its origin story centres on a sacred cave, which the shrine opens to visitors on the 1st and 15th of each month.

    Look for Royal-patronage shrine of the Ryūkyū Eight, with a sacred cave

    4-1-43 Hantagawa, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Kotobank, SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives)

  40. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Naha

    Arakaki Chinsukō Honpo, Kokusai-dōri Makishi (新垣ちんすこう本舗 牧志店)

    The Kokusai-dōri shop of the old Ryūkyū confectioner whose line goes back to Arakaki Shukiki, a royal-kitchen cook at Shuri Castle. Its founder is credited with turning chinsukō from a steamed cake into the baked biscuit sold today, and the shop still makes it by hand. Listed by OCVB, Mapple and Rurubu.

    1-3-68 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  41. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Takara Shokudō, Wakasa (高良食堂)

    A neighbourhood shokudō in the residential streets behind Wakasa beach, serving Okinawan home cooking. Its champurū is seasoned with miso for a gentle taste, and the clear soup of pork bone and bonito is its most praised point. Listed by OCVB, Mapple and Rurubu.

    1-7-10 Wakasa, Naha, Okinawa 900-0031, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  42. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Naha

    Sennichi (千日)

    Naha's classic zenzai parlour near Naminoue Shrine, in business since the 1950s (the founders' Yafune Shokudo, then 'Sennichi' in Kume from 1962). Order the Okinawa zenzai: plump, slow-stewed beans under a triangle of hand-shaved ice.

    Kume, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), macaroni (macaro-ni.jp), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  43. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Naha

    Steakhouse 88 Tsuji Honten (ステーキハウス88 辻本店)

    Flagship of the Steakhouse 88 chain, descended from 'CLUB88', an A-sign restaurant licensed for US personnel in 1955. Neon diner room, 20-plus steak cuts, open till 1 am — the classic Okinawan 'shime' (end-of-night) steak.

    2-8-21 Tsuji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Okinawatraveler, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  44. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Pork Tamago Onigiri Honten, Makishi (ポークたまごおにぎり本店)

    The flagship of the 'Pōtama' shop that turned Okinawa's pork-and-egg onigiri into a takeaway icon; each one is pressed to order so the rice is hot and the egg fluffy. Opens early (7:00) for breakfast, closed Wednesdays.

    2-8-35 Matsuo, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  45. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Naha

    Ryūkyū no Shuki to Awamori Oninoude, Tsuboya (琉球ノ酒器ト泡盛 オニノウデ)

    Awamori bar opened in July 2016 by sake-vessel collector Sakukawa Nagamasa, about 10 minutes' walk from Kokusai-dōri toward the Nōren market; some 400 awamori, many from the outer islands, poured from Okinawan karakara/chibugwā flasks and works by noted potters. Named for the long 'ogre's arm' bottle of old Ryūkyū; picked in BRUTUS's Naha bar issue.

    1-7-13 Tsuboya, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Okinawaclip, Brutus (Magazine House), Syugyoku

  46. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Naha

    Daitō Soba Kokusai-dōri (大東そば 国際通り店)

    Near Midorigaoka Park off Kokusai-dōri, the one place in Naha serving the Minami-Daitō Island soul food: thick curly noodles meant to evoke the island's rough seas, in a light pork broth, with Daitō-zushi. The owner spent a year recreating the original shop's recipe after it closed in 2022 and kept its logo.

    1-2-17 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Tabirai

  47. Worth the detour · Wagyu, Yakiniku & Sukiyaki · Naha

    Yappari Steak 1st, Cocktail Plaza (やっぱりステーキ 1st カクテルプラザ店)

    The founding store of the Okinawa-born steak chain: it opened in Matsuyama in February 2015 as a six-seat counter selling a ¥1,000 steak, drew queues by word of mouth and grew into a nationwide chain of some 90 shops within eight years (profiled on TV Tokyo's Cambria Palace). Continues Okinawa's post-war steak-dinner culture.

    Cocktail Plaza 1F, 1-34-3 Matsuyama, Naha, Okinawa 〒900-0032

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), TV Tokyo — Cambria Palace (カンブリア宮殿), Official Site

  48. Worth the detour · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Naha

    Live House Shimauta, Kokusai-dōri (ライブハウス島唄)

    Home stage of Nēnēs, the women's vocal group credited with sparking the shima-uta boom; they play several nights a week (three sets a night), with other local acts on the rest. Okinawan food and drink served, no time limit on the live charge.

    Haisai Okinawa Bldg 3F, 1-2-31 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Official Site

  49. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Teshiraji Soba, Shuri (てぃしらじそば 汀志良次)

    A small soba shop on Route 82, about halfway between Shuri and Gibo monorail stations. It takes its name from the old village of Tishiraji. The owner, who quit an office job to open it, makes and hand-rubs the curly noodles from the day before and serves them in a very clear broth topped with needle ginger rather than red pickled ginger. It closes when the soba sells out.

    1-1 Shuri Teira-chō, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Tabirai, Okinawaclip

  50. Worth the detour · Naha

    Sonohyan-utaki Ishimon (園比屋武御嶽石門)

    Stone gate to the sacred grove behind it, where Ryūkyū kings prayed for safe journeys before leaving Shuri; a UNESCO component standing beside Shuri Castle Park.

    Look for Sacred stone gate

    Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Visit Okinawa

  51. Worth the detour · Naha

    Naminoue Shrine (波上宮)

    Okinawa’s ichinomiya (chief shrine), perched on a coral bluff above Naminoue Beach; long the place where fishermen and sailors prayed for a safe voyage.

    Look for Clifftop chief shrine of Okinawa

    Wakasa, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives)

  52. Worth the detour · Naha

    Sakaemachi Market (栄町市場)

    Showa-era covered market by Asato station: groceries by day, and after dark a warren of tiny bars and izakaya where locals drink on stools in the alleys.

    Look for Retro market & bar alleys

    381 Asato, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  53. Worth the detour · Naha

    Fukushū-en Garden (福州園)

    Walled Chinese garden opened in 1992 for Naha's sister city Fuzhou, built with materials shipped from Fujian — pagoda over a waterfall, ponds and moon gates in old Kume, the Chinese scholars' quarter.

    Look for Chinese walled garden

    Kume, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Visit Okinawa

  54. Worth the detour · Naha

    Tsuboya Pottery Museum (那覇市立壺屋焼物博物館)

    Municipal museum on Yachimun-dōri with some 7,000 pieces — from a 6,700-year-old shard through Ryūkyū-kingdom wares to today's masters — plus a preserved climbing kiln.

    Look for Pottery museum

    1-9-32 Tsuboya, Naha, Okinawa 902-0065, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  55. Worth the detour · Naha

    Benzaitendō & Enkaku-ji, Shuri (弁財天堂・円覚寺跡)

    Islet hall to the goddess of sea voyages in Enkan-chi pond, opposite the gate of Enkaku-ji — the royal family temple whose National Treasures were lost in 1945.

    Look for Royal temple & pond hall

    Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  56. Worth the detour · Naha

    Sueyoshi-gū Shrine & Sueyoshi Park (末吉宮)

    One of the Eight Shrines of the Ryūkyū Kingdom, perched on a forested limestone ridge in Sueyoshi Park; a stone path climbs through jungle to the rebuilt hall — a quiet counterpoint to Shuri Castle.

    Look for Ryukyu-kingdom shrine in forest park

    Sueyoshi-chō, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives)

  57. Worth the detour · Naha

    Sōgen-ji Stone Gate (崇元寺石門)

    The surviving stone gate of the Ryūkyū royal temple founded in 1527, where all who entered — even the king — had to dismount; the temple was destroyed in WWII but the gate was restored and has been an Important Cultural Property since 1972, fronting a small park.

    Your guide’s note Ryukyu royal temple gate (Important Cultural Property)

    Tomari, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives)

  58. Worth the detour · Naha

    Naminoue Beach & Naminoue Umisora Park (波の上ビーチ・波の上うみそら公園)

    Naha's only city beach, sitting below the cliff-top Naminoue Shrine, with free entry and swimming from mid-April to October. The adjoining Umisora Park's enclosed man-made bay is a favourite with people learning to dive.

    Look for City beach below Naminoue Shrine

    1-25 Wakasa, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  59. Worth the detour · Naha

    Sugar Loaf Hill (シュガーローフ / 安里52高地)

    The low hill the US Marines called Sugar Loaf and the Japanese 'Asato Hill 52', locally Kerama-chiiji, was fought over by the 6th Marine Division and the Japanese 32nd Army in May 1945. Today it is the Asato reservoir park beside Omoromachi monorail station, with an inscribed marker amid the new city centre.

    Look for Battle of Okinawa hill in the middle of Shintoshin

    1-6 Omoromachi, Naha, Okinawa (Asato Haisuichi Park)

    Recommended by Wiki, Naha City (official municipal publications)

  60. Worth the detour · Naha

    Gokoku-ji Temple, Naminoue (護国寺)

    Shingon temple founded in 1367 beside Naminoue Shrine, once the Ryūkyū Kingdom's royal prayer temple and head of Shingon in the kingdom. Missionary Bernard Bettelheim occupied it 1846–1853, and its 1465 bell was given to Commodore Perry (long kept at Annapolis).

    Look for Ryūkyū royal temple · Bettelheim & Perry's bell

    1-25-5 Wakasa, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Wiki, SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives)

  61. Worth the detour · Naha

    Okinogū Shrine, Onoyama Park (沖宮)

    One of the Ryūkyū Hassha, dedicated to Kumano Gongen and long prayed to for safe voyages by tribute ships. Founded beside Naha harbour (per the 1713 Ryūkyū-koku Yuraiki), designated a National Treasure in 1935, destroyed in 1945, re-established in 1961 and moved to Onoyama Park in 1975.

    Look for Ryūkyū's harbour shrine for safe voyages, rebuilt in Onoyama Park

    44 Ōnoyama-chō, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives)

  62. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Naha

    Zuisen Distillery (瑞泉酒造)

    Shuri awamori maker descended from the distillers who supplied the royal court; free tour of the stills and fermentation tanks, a look into the kusu ageing cellar and a tasting of Zuisen and Omoro.

    1-35 Sakiyama-cho, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

    Round-the-clock homestyle shokudō near the Prefectural Office: gōyā champurū, spam and egg, and the house 'chanpon' — Okinawa's stir-fry-on-rice take — in a room that feels like grandma's kitchen.

    Matsuyama, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

    Soba in an old Okinawan house in Kokuba; the 'special' piles on soki, belly and the owner's prized tebichi. On the Okinawa Times 2023 reader-poll list.

    City-run crafts centre on Kokusai-dōri with exhibition rooms, a shop and hands-on workshops for five Naha traditional crafts, including Ryūkyū glass, bingata, Shuri-ori weaving, lacquerware and Tsuboya pottery. Featured on the OCVB's Naha traditional-crafts walking course.

    Shima-uta to Jiryōri Tubarama, Kokusai-dōri (島唄と地料理 とぅばらーま)

    An Okinawan-cuisine restaurant on Kokusai-dōri, a one-minute walk from Makishi Station, with an interior that recreates a pre-war Okinawan townscape. Lunch is Okinawa soba and chanpurū set meals, and sanshin shima-uta (island-song) bands play every night. OTV Okitive featured it for blending tradition with modern twists such as an Okinawan-style fried rice.

    2-7-25 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Tabirai, Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  78. Deep cut · Naha

    Great Akagi Trees of Shuri Kinjō (首里金城の大アカギ)

    A grove of six huge akagi (Bischofia) trees and one Ryūkyū hackberry behind the Uchikanagusuku shrine just off the Kinjō-chō stone road, designated a national Natural Monument in 1972; the largest is 5.2 m round and 13 m tall. No other such grove of giant akagi survives in a settled area of Okinawa.

    Look for National Natural Monument grove off the stone road

    3-18-20 Shuri Kinjō-chō, Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Agency For Cultural Affairs, Tabimag, Ocvb

  79. Deep cut · Naha

    Mekaru Tomb Site, Shintoshin (銘苅墓跡群)

    National Historic Site (2007): a hillside necropolis of 330+ tombs spanning the Gusuku era through the Ryūkyū Kingdom to Meiji, the oldest from the 14th–15th c.; its largest turtleback tomb is 22 m wide and 30 m deep. Survived the build-out of Naha Shintoshin.

    Look for National Historic Site · 330 Ryūkyū tombs in the new city centre

    Mekaru 2-chōme (hill opposite the Naha City Fire Department HQ), Naha, Okinawa

    Recommended by Agency For Cultural Affairs, Wiki, Kotobank

  80. Deep cut · Naha

    Naha's original Pokémon manhole cover, an Arcanine design on the OCVB 'Flying Pikachu' Poké Lid trail, set in Tenbusu Plaza on Kokusai-dōri. In April 2026 a photo of it covered by pipe chairs during an event drew more than 24 million views. Naha City then said it was considering moving the lid and was in talks with The Pokémon Company. Check it is still here before you go.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids / Flying Pikachu Project) — Naha's Arcanine lid; went viral in 2026 when buried under event chairs (relocation under review) · Viral Pokémon manhole on Kokusai-dōri

    Tenbusu Plaza (Tenbusu Naha), 3-2 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Jprime, Ocvb

  81. Deep cut · Naha

    Mie Gusuku Fort (三重城)

    Gusuku built by King Shō Sei in 1546 on the north mouth of Naha harbour, paired with Yarazamori Gusuku to guard the port and town. A coast-guard watchtower stands on it today, but the stone site is open to the public as a sea-view lookout.

    Look for 1546 harbour fort, now a quiet sunset lookout

    3 Nishi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Shirobito (城びと) — castle portal, Retrip (rtrp.jp) travel magazine

    Ameku-gū Shrine, Tomari (天久宮)

    One of the Ryūkyū Hassha, founded in the Chenghua era (1465–87) and enshrining Izanami with Hayatamao and Kotosakao (the Kumano deities); annual festival on 15 May. Tucked into a hillside in Tomari.

    Look for Hillside Kumano shrine of the Ryūkyū Eight in Tomari

    3-19-3 Tomari, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Jinjacho, SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives)

    Recommended by Ocvb, Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  98. Deep cut · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Yuunami Sakashita (自家製生麺 ゆうなみ 坂下店)

    A local Okinawa-soba shop whose house-made fresh noodles are blended with whole-wheat flour. You can pick thin, flat or mugwort noodles for the signature nankotsu sōki soba, and the pork-and-bonito broth is rich enough to drink to the last drop. Readers voted it into the Okinawa Times 2023 '900 noodle lovers pick' Okinawa-soba ranking (southern edition).

    Terrace Sakashita 1F, 301-15 Matsukawa, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive

  99. Deep cut · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Soba-dokoro Kikuya, Oroku (そば処 きくや)

    A red-tiled house next to the owner's home, about five minutes by car from Naha Airport. The light broth of pork bone, bonito, kombu and vegetables is simmered for two days. The menu has sanmai-niku soba, yushi-tōfu soba and black-sugar zenzai, and it closes when sold out (around 3 pm). It was picked in the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll of Okinawa-soba shops (southern edition).

    1-6-2 Tahara, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Tabirai

  100. Deep cut · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Okinawa Jiryōri Angama, Kokusai-dōri (沖縄地料理 あんがま)

    An Okinawan-cuisine and folk-song restaurant just inside the south entrance of Kokusai-dōri. The entrance is built like a red-tiled, stone-walled house and is topped by a giant mask from Ishigaki's Angama Bon festival. The menu has about 60 dishes made with island vegetables, pork and local seafood, including gōyā chanpurū, tebichi and sōki-ni, plus four set courses. Min'yō singers play every night in the third-floor hall.

    1-2-2 Matsuo, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawatraveler, Tabirai

  101. Deep cut · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Naha

    Sakaemachi Kai Senmon Sakaba Hiikiya (栄町貝専門酒場 ひいき屋)

    A red-lantern counter bar in Sakaemachi Market that serves only shellfish. It usually has 25 or more kinds of seasonal shellfish from around Japan and Okinawa, rising past 35 at peak season. The counter faces the market lane, and Tabirai describes it as a place where you easily get talking to locals ('ichariba chōdē').

    379 Asato, Naha, Okinawa 902-0067, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Tabirai

  102. Deep cut · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Naha

    Okinawa Soba Senmonten Charu Soba, Sakaemachi (沖縄そば専門店 ちゃるそば)

    An Okinawa-soba specialist inside Sakaemachi Market. Okinawa Times called its cloudy, bonito-scented broth 'one of a kind'. Soft-bone sōki and pork-belly soba come with jūshī rice, and the evening menu adds a senbero drinks set.

    388-1 Asato (Sakaemachi Market), Naha, Okinawa 902-0067, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Feeljapan

  103. Closed — kept for the record · Naha

    Naha City Museum of History (那覇市歴史博物館) — CLOSED

    Opened in 2006 to show the National Treasure 'Materials related to the Shō Family of Ryūkyū Kings' (1,166 documents and 85 art objects, including the royal crown). It closed on 31 August 2025; the treasures are due to be shown at the former Nakagusuku Udun site, opening date not yet set.

    Look for Closed Aug 2025 — home of the Shō royal National Treasures

    Palette Kumoji 4F, 1-1-1 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Wiki, Agency For Cultural Affairs, Nahanavi

Chūbu 85

Central Okinawa (Chatan & American Village · Okinawa City/Koza · Ginowan · Urasoe · Yomitan

  1. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Chūbu

    Jimmy's Ōyama (ジミー 大山店)

    The first shop of Jimmy's, the American-style bakery, deli and import grocery founded in 1956 and loved by Okinawans ever since. Its fresh-baked pies, apple pie above all, cream puffs and other pastries are the draw, alongside imported groceries, wine and awamori.

    2-22-5 Ōyama, Ginowan, Okinawa

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Japan Travel (japantravel.com), Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  2. Must see · International & Fusion · Chūbu

    Cafe Ocean, Gate 2 Street (カフェ オーシャン)

    Founded in 1967, Ocean is the oldest taco shop on Koza's Gate 2 Street in front of Kadena Air Base, frying hand-made tortillas to order with a home-style sauce taught by Americans. A taco-and-music café-bar from the post-war 'A-sign' era.

    2-15-2 Chūō, Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-0004, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Ocvb, KozaWeb — Okinawa City Tourism Portal

  3. Must see · Chūbu

    Pokémon Center Okinawa, Aeon Mall Okinawa Rycom (ポケモンセンターオキナワ)

    Okinawa's first Pokémon Center (opened 11 Aug 2022, Japan's 16th), themed on the island's nature: Pikachu and Arcanine greet you at the entrance, with Okinawa-only goods and a video zone. Pair it with a hunt for the prefecture's 16 Pokémon manhole 'Poké Lids'.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon — the prefecture's only Pokémon Center, with Okinawa-exclusive merchandise · Pokémon flagship store

    Aeon Mall Okinawa Rycom 1F, 1 Raikamu, Kitanakagusuku, Okinawa 901-2306, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Game Watch (Impress Watch), Official Site

  4. Must see · Chūbu

    Nakamura House (中村家住宅)

    A wealthy farmer's homestead built in the 1720s — the island's prime surviving example of early-modern Okinawan domestic architecture, with red-tiled roofs, a coral-stone wall and fukugi-tree windbreak; a National Important Cultural Property near Nakagusuku Castle.

    Look for 18th-century Ryūkyū farmhouse

    106 Ōshiro, Kitanakagusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives), Japan Experience, Japan Travel (japantravel.com)

  5. Must see · Chūbu

    Sakima Art Museum (佐喜眞美術館)

    Private museum opened in 1994 on land reclaimed from a corner of US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma. Its centrepiece is Iri and Toshi Maruki's 4 × 8.5 m 'Battle of Okinawa' panel, painted from survivors' testimony by the artists of the Hiroshima Panels.

    Look for The Marukis' Battle of Okinawa mural beside Futenma

    1-22 Uehara, Ginowan, Okinawa 901-2204, Japan

    Recommended by Wiki, Ocvb, Ginowancity

  6. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Chūbu

    Hamaya Soba (そば専門店 浜屋)

    Soba specialist by the Sunabe seawall, a local and tourist favourite for its soft-boned cartilage soki in a clean, salt-seasoned broth.

    Sunabe, Chatan, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawa Times

  7. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Chūbu

    Blue Seal Makiminato Honten (ブルーシール 牧港本店)

    'Born in America, raised in Okinawa': Blue Seal started in 1948 supplying the US bases and moved to this Makiminato drive-in in 1963. The flagship was rebuilt and reopened in 2024 to a 400-person queue — order beni-imo or salt-chinsukō.

    5-5-6 Makiminato, Urasoe, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler

  8. Must see · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Chūbu

    Shinzato Distillery (新里酒造)

    Founded in 1846, Shinzato is one of the oldest operating awamori distilleries in Okinawa, now run by the seventh-generation owner. It offers a roughly 45-minute factory tour combining traditional craft and modern technology, and has won the awamori grand prize at the All Japan sake competition.

    12-17 Suzaki, Uruma, Okinawa 904-2234, Japan (head office 3-22-8 Koja, Okinawa City)

    Recommended by Ocvb, Walkerplus (kadokawa Walker magazines), KozaWeb — Okinawa City Tourism Portal

  9. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Chūbu

    Hanaori Soba, Yomitan (花織そば)

    Yomitan's flagship Okinawa-soba house on Prefectural Road 6, founded in 1988 by a former French-cuisine chef. The signature bowl tops medium-thin wavy noodles in pork-bone broth with soft-bone sōki and long-simmered pork belly; tebichi and liver-and-nira soba are also on the menu. It reopened after a renovation in 2026.

    2418-1 Hanza, Yomitan, Okinawa 904-0322, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Ocvb, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  10. Must see · Chūbu

    Nakagusuku Castle (中城城跡)

    Best-preserved of the Ryūkyū castle ruins: six enclosures of curved limestone walls on a ridge above both coasts. UNESCO Gusuku component.

    Look for Gusuku ruins

    Nakagusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Wikipedia

  11. Must see · Chūbu

    Yomitan Yachimun no Sato Pottery Village (やちむんの里)

    Lane of red-tile workshops and climbing kilns founded after Living National Treasure Jiro Kinjo moved his studio here in 1972; around 45–50 potters, with shops selling cups, plates and shisa.

    Look for Pottery village

    Zakimi, Yomitan, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  12. Must see · Chūbu

    Mihama American Village (美浜アメリカンビレッジ)

    Reclaimed-land entertainment district with a Ferris wheel, Depot Island's colourful facades, US-style diners and boutiques — the clearest expression of Chatan's base-town melting pot.

    Look for Base-town shopping & dining district

    Mihama, Chatan, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  13. Must see · Chūbu

    Koza Gate 2 Street (コザ ゲート通り)

    The street running to Kadena Air Base's Gate 2, Okinawa's live-music strip since the 1960s–70s: rock, blues and Latin bars alongside Okinawan folk; home of the November International Carnival.

    Look for Live-music nightlife street

    Chuo, Okinawa City, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  14. Must see · Chūbu

    Kaichū-dōro sea causeway (海中道路)

    Five-kilometre road laid across turquoise shallows from the Katsuren Peninsula to Henza, then bridged on to Hamahiga, Miyagi and Ikei — the island-hop drive of central Okinawa.

    Look for Sea causeway drive

    Yonashiro, Uruma, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  15. Must see · Chūbu

    Kakazu Ridge — Kakazu Takadai Park (嘉数高台公園)

    One of the fiercest battlefields of the 1945 Battle of Okinawa: US forces attacked Kakazu Ridge on 9 April 1945 and needed about 15 days to take it, with thousands dead on both sides. Today a hilltop park with a globe-shaped observation deck looking over Futenma Air Station and toward the Maeda Escarpment, plus surviving pillboxes.

    Look for WWII battlefield & lookout

    Kakazu, Ginowan, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Pacific Wrecks (wwii sites database)

  16. Must see · Chūbu

    Minatogawa Stateside Town (港川ステイツサイドタウン)

    A neighbourhood of 1950s–60s white single-storey 'foreign houses' built for US military families, now converted into cafés, bakeries, galleries and shops. Lanes are named after US states (Oregon, Arizona, Michigan, Kansas and more); about 5 minutes' walk from the Minatogawa bus stop.

    Look for Retro US-housing café district

    around 2-17 Minatogawa, Urasoe, Okinawa 901-2134, Japan

    Recommended by Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Ana Japan Travel Planner

  17. Must see · International & Fusion · Chūbu

    Mexico, Chatan (タコス専門店 メキシコ)

    Taco-only shop serving since 1977 — one of the island's most famous taco joints, crisp shells stuffed with seasoned beef in the style US servicemen brought to Okinawa.

    Chatan, Nakagami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  18. Must see · International & Fusion · Chūbu

    Charlie's Tacos, Koza (チャーリー多幸寿)

    Koza taco counter a short walk from Kadena's Gate 2 where locals, mainlanders and Americans have queued for more than 60 years — one of the A-sign-era base-town originals.

    Chuo, Okinawa City, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, KozaWeb — Okinawa City Tourism Portal

  19. Must see · Wagyu, Yakiniku & Sukiyaki · Chūbu

    Teppanyaki Steak House Shiki, Sonoda Honten (ステーキハウス四季 園田本店)

    A Koza teppanyaki steak house running for close to half a century in the post-war steak heartland by Kadena; chefs sear the steak on the iron in front of you.

    Sonoda, Okinawa City, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by KozaWeb — Okinawa City Tourism Portal, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  20. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Chūbu

    oHacorté Minatogawa Honten (オハコルテ 港川本店)

    The fruit-tart shop (founded 2009) that made Minatogawa's 'Stateside Town' — some thirty shops and cafés in converted 1950s US military housing — a destination; glossy seasonal tarts in a little white house.

    #18, 2-17-1 Minatogawa, Urasoe, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  21. Must see · International & Fusion · Chūbu

    Tacos-ya Chatan (タコス屋 北谷店)

    Small taco shop on a backstreet near the Sunabe Seawall that has fed locals and visitors for about 35 years; it still fries its house-made shells to order for a chewy-crisp texture, and its Tacos-ya Plate piles tacos, taco rice, onion rings and fries on one plate.

    1-5 Miyagi, Chatan, Okinawa, Japan (near the Sunabe Seawall)

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Walkerplus (kadokawa Walker magazines)

  22. Must see · Teishoku, Curry & Yōshoku · Chūbu

    Pizza House Honten, Urasoe (ピザハウス 本店)

    Founded in 1958 (its founders served Okinawa's first pizza), this American-style restaurant near Minatogawa Stateside Town is known for its roast beef and steaks. The main branch reopened in a 1950s-diner-style renovation on 15 March 2026 with the stated aim of becoming a '100-year restaurant'.

    2-20-5 Minatogawa, Urasoe, Okinawa 901-2134, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報)

  23. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Chūbu

    Tsurukame-dō Zenzai, Yomitan (鶴亀堂ぜんざい)

    Zenzai shop near Zakimi Castle serving Okinawa-style zenzai — kintoki beans simmered for six hours under fluffy shaved ice. Its signature uses Yomitan's own beni-imo purple sweet potato, which dyes the ice violet under a brown-sugar syrup.

    248-1 Zakimi, Yomitan, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler

  24. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    Poké Lid — Growlithe over Mihama fireworks, Depot Island Boardwalk, Chatan (ポケふた ガーディ 北谷町美浜)

    A Pokémon manhole cover installed in August 2025 at the seaside boardwalk of Depot Island in Mihama. It shows Growlithe, Okinawa's 'support Pokémon', against American Village's night skyline and fireworks. It sits just before the boardwalk steps, which is also a popular fireworks-viewing spot. It is one of four Growlithe lids the Pokémon Company gave to Okinawan towns in 2025.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids / Pokémon Local Acts) — Growlithe, Okinawa's 'support Pokémon', over American Village fireworks · Pokémon manhole on the boardwalk

    Depot Island Boardwalk (seaside), 9-1 Mihama, Chatan Town, Okinawa 904-0115, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Qab Ryukyu Asahi Broadcasting (琉球朝日放送) news, Chatantourism, Ocvb, 4Gamer.net (game/pop-culture news of record)

  25. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    National Theatre Okinawa (国立劇場おきなわ)

    Opened 18 January 2004 as Japan's fifth national theatre, built to preserve and present Okinawan traditional performing arts — above all kumiodori, the Ryukyuan court music-drama. A 632-seat main hall and a 255-seat small hall.

    Look for Home stage of kumiodori

    4-14-1 Jitchaku, Urasoe, Okinawa

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Tabimag, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Official Site

  26. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    Shirumichu sacred cave, Hamahiga Island (シルミチュー霊場)

    A limestone cave up a 108-step stair behind a torii on Hamahiga Island, held to be where the Ryūkyū creator deities Shinerikyo and Amamikyo lived and raised their children — a place of prayer for fertility and harvest. The cave itself is normally closed and opened for Lunar New Year rites.

    Look for Cave home of the creator gods

    near 1606-3 Katsuren-Higa, Uruma, Okinawa

    Recommended by Okinawaclip, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Ocvb, nippon.com (Nippon Communications Foundation)

  27. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Chūbu

    Highway Drive-In Restaurant, Okinawa City (ハイウェイ食堂)

    Opened in 1972 by a US Army cook as an A-sign establishment and seemingly frozen in time since: huge diner plates, low prices, fast service, open till 2 am on Route 75.

    Route 75, Okinawa City, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by KozaWeb — Okinawa City Tourism Portal, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Japan Travel (japantravel.com), Okinawatraveler

  28. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Chūbu

    Gordie's, Sunabe (ゴーディーズ)

    Stand By Me-themed burger joint in a converted former on-base house near the Sunabe Seawall, serving coarse-ground, filler-free charcoal-grilled patties since 2007. Its Special Burger stacks two patties, thick bacon, a fried egg and cheese.

    100 Sunabe, Chatan, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, macaroni (macaro-ni.jp), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  29. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Chūbu

    TESIO, Koza Gate Street (テシオ)

    A ham-and-sausage maker on Koza's Gate Street, opened April 2017 by an Okinawan trained in German charcuterie methods; its products have won gold medals at IFFA, the German international meat-processing competition. Sausages are made by hand daily and a weekend hot-dog counter serves them in-shop.

    1-10-3 Chūō, Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-0004, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Smartmagazine, Tabirai, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報)

  30. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    Bios Hill (ビオスの丘)

    A nature theme park in Uruma's Ishikawa hills: water-buffalo cart rides, lake boat rides through subtropical forest and orchid viewing; you can also try on Ryukyu-era costume. Stars and Stripes Okinawa has covered it repeatedly as a family day out.

    Look for Water-buffalo carts & jungle lake

    Ishikawa-Kadekaru, Uruma, Okinawa

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Feeljapan, Official Site

  31. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    Urasoe Art Museum (浦添市美術館)

    Opened in 1990 as Japan's first museum devoted to lacquer art and Okinawa's first public art museum. Its collection centres on Ryukyu lacquerware from the 16th century to today, with 80–100 pieces on show in themed displays that change three times a year; the building is by architect Uchii Shōzō.

    Look for Japan's first lacquer-art museum

    1-9-2 Nakama, Urasoe, Okinawa

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Official Site, Walkerplus (kadokawa Walker magazines)

  32. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    Urasoe Yōdore Royal Mausoleum & Urasoe Castle ruins (浦添ようどれ・浦添城跡)

    Cliffside royal tombs carved under King Eiso in 1261, below the ridge of Urasoe Castle, seat of the early Chūzan kings. The ridge was a Japanese defensive line in 1945 and the tombs, badly damaged, were later restored; free entry and parking, ~15 min walk from Urasoe-Maeda monorail station.

    Look for 13th-century royal tombs

    2-53-1 Nakama, Urasoe, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wiki, SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives), Okinawa Urban Monorail (Yui Rail) official navi

  33. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    Plaza House Shopping Center (プラザハウス ショッピングセンター)

    Billed as Japan's first shopping center, opened in 1954 to serve officers and families of the nearby US Ryukyu Command HQ. Its mid-century three-storey atrium and single-storey arcade survive, now holding an international food market, cafés, bakeries, interiors stores and Okinawan crafts; it appears in the Agency for Cultural Affairs' survey of Okinawa's modern architecture.

    Look for 1954 American-era mall

    Okinawa City, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Ocvb, Bunka Survey

  34. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    Southeast Botanical Gardens (東南植物楽園)

    One of Japan's largest outdoor botanical gardens, with about 1,300 species and over 50,000 plants, and a nationally Registered Monument. Seasonal night illuminations draw crowds in winter.

    Look for Japan's big outdoor tropical garden

    2146 Chibana, Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-2143, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, KozaWeb — Okinawa City Tourism Portal, Tabirai

  35. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    Koza Music Town (コザ・ミュージックタウン)

    Okinawa City's 'town of music' hub, opened in 2007 at the Koza crossroads as part of the city's music-led regeneration: the Ongaku Ichiba (Music Town Ongaku Ichiba) live hall, studios and a music plaza that hosts events tied to the All-Island Eisa Festival.

    Look for Hub of Koza's rock and min'yō scene

    1-1-1 Uechi, Okinawa City, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Ocvb, KozaWeb — Okinawa City Tourism Portal

  36. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Chūbu

    RuLer's TACORiCE Ginowan Honten (ルーラーズタコライス 宜野湾本店)

    A taco-rice specialist whose Ginowan flagship serves eight original recipes — classic cheese, BBQ, Caesar, teriyaki and the avocado-bacon-cheese ABC — in sizes up to extra-large, with about ten extra toppings. Tabirai lists it among Okinawa's nine top taco-rice shops.

    3-8-2 Maehara, Ginowan, Okinawa

    Recommended by Tabirai, macaroni (macaro-ni.jp), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  37. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Chūbu

    A&W Makiminato (A&W 牧港店)

    A&W came to Okinawa in 1963, years before mainland Japan — the 24-hour Makiminato drive-in on Route 58 is the chain's Okinawa flagship. Root beer in a frosted mug, curly fries and a burger is a rite of passage.

    4-9-1 Makiminato, Urasoe, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Japan Travel (japantravel.com), Okinawatraveler

  38. Worth the detour · Markets, Depachika & Street Food · Chūbu

    Nuchi Māsu Salt Factory, Miyagi Island (ぬちまーす観光製塩ファクトリー)

    Clifftop salt works across the Kaichū-dōro on Miyagi Island, where a patented spray-drying method snows mineral-rich salt inside the factory; free 10-minute tours every 20 minutes, a sea-view restaurant and shop.

    2768 Miyagi, Yonashiro, Uruma, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler

  39. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Chūbu

    Miyanchi STUDIO & COFFEE, Okinawa City (みやんち STUDIO&COFFEE)

    Red-tiled café and studio opened in 2012 in the hills of Okinawa City, produced by THE BOOM singer Kazufumi Miyazawa to share Okinawan folk music and food. Its signature is kara-soba, a soup-less Okinawa soba Miyazawa devised after eating a version on Ishigaki.

    1-29-22 Yogi, Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-2174, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawatraveler, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Walkerplus (kadokawa Walker magazines)

  40. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Chūbu

    Player's Cafe, Koza (プレイヤーズカフェ)

    Opened in 1999 on Koza's Park Avenue, this café hosts live music of all genres and doubles as the lounge of Tripshot Hotels Koza; its menu draws on the owner's memories of 1970s Koza home cooking shaped by US-military canned goods. Ryukyu Shimpo reported its lunch sets as a hit with a wide range of customers.

    2-6-47 Chūō (Park Avenue), Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-0004, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), KozaWeb — Okinawa City Tourism Portal

  41. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Chūbu

    Zhyvago Coffee Works Okinawa, Chatan (ジバゴコーヒーワークス)

    A West Coast-style coffee stand on the Mihama seafront, opened in 2015, that makes each cup to order. The Ryukyu Shimpo profiled Kotaro Mikami, the Chatan Zhyvago shop manager, as the Japan AeroPress Championship winner. The brand also co-developed a coffee with JTA airline to go with chinsukō.

    Distortion Seaside Bldg, 9-46 Mihama, Chatan-chō, Nakagami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Okinawa Times

  42. Worth the detour · Wagyu, Yakiniku & Sukiyaki · Chūbu

    Sam's Anchor Inn Ginowan (サムズアンカーイン 宜野湾店)

The Ryukyu Shimpo marked the chain's 55th anniversary in 2025.

Gushikawa Beach appears in episode 2 and other walk-to-school scenes, and pilgrims start from the Gushikawa Community Hall, which hands out Uruma's official location map and has one of three Okitsura manhole covers (the others are at KIN Sunrise Beach and Michi-no-Eki Ginoza).

  52. Worth the detour · Chūbu

    Chibichiri Gama (チビチリガマ)

    A natural cave near the US landing beaches where, in April 1945, 140 villagers sheltered as American forces approached and 83 died in a forced mass suicide. A memorial stands at the mouth; the cave itself is closed to entry out of respect, and memorial services are held each spring.

    Look for WWII memorial cave (view from outside)

    Namihira, Yomitan, Okinawa, Japan

    Okinawa Zoo & Museum — Okinawa Kodomo no Kuni (沖縄こどもの国)

    Japan's southernmost zoo and the only one in the prefecture, reopened in 2004 with a child-focused layout: Nature Land (the zoo, with Yanbaru and Okinawan native species), the three-storey hands-on Wonder Museum and a Children's Center with petting animals.

    Futenma-gū Shrine & cave (普天満宮)

    One of the Ryūkyū Eight Shrines granted special status by the kingdom; it began as worship of an indigenous deity in its cave, with Kumano Gongen enshrined in the mid-15th century. The 280 m limestone cave behind the hall, where 3,000-year-old artefacts were excavated, is a Ginowan city Place of Scenic Beauty and can be visited.

    Look for Ryūkyū Eight Shrines member with a sacred cave

    Opened in 1975 as a restaurant with a take-out window, on the site where Michi-no-Eki Kadena stands now. Its American-style menu was a rarity that won over locals and visitors. The founders' daughter took over in 2016; the dining room closed after the renovation and the pandemic, and it now runs as a take-out counter on the roadside station's ground floor, famous for its jumbo cheeseburger.

    1F Michi-no-Eki Kadena, 1026-3 Yara, Kadena, Okinawa
