Nanbu 52

Southern Okinawa (Itoman · Nanjō & Sēfa-utaki · Peace Memorial Park · Tomigusuku

  1. Must see · Nanbu

    Kudaka Island (久高島)

    The 'island of the gods', 5.3 km off Cape Chinen: in Ryūkyū belief the creator goddess Amamikyo descended here, and kings once made pilgrimage to it. A slender 1.38 km² island reached by ferry from Azama port, explored by bicycle; some sacred groves are off-limits.

    Look for Sacred island (ferry from Azama)

    Kudaka, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wiki, Visit Okinawa, SamuraiWiki (Samurai-Archives)

  2. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Nanbu

    Yagiya (屋宜家)

    Soba served in a registered cultural-property red-tiled house; choose classic, soy-milk or seaweed noodles in a light but deep bonito broth.

    1172 Ōgan, Yaese, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawatraveler, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  3. Must see · Markets, Depachika & Street Food · Nanbu

    Itoman Fishermen's Co-op Osakana Center, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (糸満漁協 お魚センター)

    Eleven fishmongers run by the Itoman fishermen's co-op inside Japan's southernmost roadside station: choose fish for a kaisendon, nigiri, fish soup or Okinawan tempura and eat on the spot, 10:00–19:00.

    4-19-1 Nishizaki, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawatraveler, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  4. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Nanbu

    Itoman Gyomin Shokudō (糸満漁民食堂)

    Fish restaurant in the fishing town of Itoman, opened in 2013 in a building of stacked Ryūkyū limestone that won a Good Design Award and JCD Design Award. Its signature is the day's local fish butter-grilled until crisp outside and tender within.

    Nishizaki, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Serai (サライ, Shogakukan magazine), All About (allabout.co.jp), Jal Skyward+ (jal in-flight magazine web)

  5. Must see · Nanbu

    Sefa-utaki (斎場御嶽)

    The holiest site of Ryūkyūan religion: a sacred grove of limestone clefts overlooking Kudaka Island, where the kingdom’s high priestess was invested. A UNESCO Gusuku component.

    Look for Most sacred utaki

    Chinen, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Wikipedia

  6. Must see · Nanbu

    Okinawa Peace Memorial Park & Prefectural Peace Memorial Museum (平和祈念公園)

    The main memorial to the Battle of Okinawa, on Mabuni Hill where the fighting ended in June 1945. The museum traces the lead-up, the battle and the rebuilding; outside, the Cornerstone of Peace lists every fallen soldier and civilian of every nationality.

    Look for Battle of Okinawa memorial & museum

    Mabuni, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  7. Must see · Nanbu

    Himeyuri Peace Museum (ひめゆり平和祈念資料館)

    Museum beside the Himeyuri Monument, telling the story of the schoolgirls drafted as nurses into army cave hospitals in 1945, most of whom died. Opened 23 June 1989.

    Look for WWII student-nurse memorial museum

    671-1 Ihara, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  8. Must see · Nanbu

    Former Japanese Navy Underground Headquarters (旧海軍司令部壕)

    Several hundred metres of hand-dug tunnels and rooms that served as the Imperial Navy's command post in 1945; the walls still bear the shrapnel marks of the officers' last stand.

    Look for WWII tunnels

    Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan (Navy HQ park, south of Naha)

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  9. Must see · Nanbu

    Okinawa World & Gyokusendo Cave (おきなわワールド 玉泉洞)

    Culture park built over Gyokusendo, a 5 km limestone cave (850 m open) — the longest in the south and second-longest in Japan — with a craft village of old houses and a habu snake museum.

    Look for Limestone cave & craft village

    Maekawa, Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  10. Must see · Nanbu

    Senaga Island & Umikaji Terrace, Tomigusuku (瀬長島ウミカジテラス)

    A small island ~600 m off the southern west coast and 1.5 km south of Naha Airport, returned by the US military in 1977; since summer 2015 its slope is lined with the white, Mediterranean-style shops and cafés of Umikaji Terrace, with planes landing overhead and sunset views.

    Look for Sunset terrace by the runway

    174-6 Senaga, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive

  11. Must see · Soba & Udon · Nanbu

    Yonabaru-ya, Yonabaru (与那原家)

    A Yonabaru soba house founded in 1985, serving homemade noodles in two broths — a light pork/chicken/bonito/kombu soup and a rich multi-bone one — with nankotsu-soki soba the most popular bowl. It was one of eight southern shops chosen in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers, and also ranks in an ITmedia Netorabo reader poll of Okinawa soba.

    1040 Yonabaru, Yonabaru-chō, Shimajiri-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, ITmedia Netorabo (ねとらぼ調査隊)

  12. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Nanbu

    Tamakaya Soba Honten (そば処 玉家 本店)

    Soba specialist prized for the balance of broth, noodles and toppings — first on the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll's southern list.

    913-1 Furugen, Ōzato, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  13. Must see · Tempura, Tonkatsu & Agemono · Nanbu

    Ganso Nakamoto Tempura, Ōjima (元祖中本てんぷら店)

    The queue-every-day tempura stand facing Ōjima fishing port, attached to a fish shop: thick-battered Okinawan tempura of fish, squid, mozuku seaweed and vegetables, eaten hot by the sea.

    9 Ōjima, Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  14. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Nanbu

    Chadokoro Makabe Chinā, Itoman (茶処 真壁ちなー)

    Soba and herb tea served in a red-tiled, stone-walled homestead whose house and grounds are a national Registered Tangible Cultural Property — the old southern-village Okinawa landscape intact.

    223 Makabe, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  15. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Nanbu

    Okinawa Soba Kintarō, Nanjō (沖縄そば 金太郎)

    A local soba shop in Tamagusuku-Funakoshi known for a rich pork-bone soup and huge 'Jirō-inspired' bowls heaped with vegetables, with a three-meat Okinawa soba as its standard. Its owner chairs the Nanjō Okinawa-soba stamp rally promoting the city as a soba town.

    1197 Funakoshi, Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa 901-0618, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Nanjotourism

  16. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Cape Chinen Park (知念岬公園)

    A grassy clifftop park at the tip of Chinen Cape, about 40 m above the sea, with a roughly 250-degree view over the reef toward Kudaka and Komaka islands, a short walk from Sefa-utaki. It is one of the settings of the 2021 anime 'The Aquatope on White Sand', the reason the Anime Tourism Association named Nanjō one of its '88 Anime Pilgrimage' sites.

    Your guide’s note ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — cape park shown in the series; Nanjō is an Anime Tourism '88' site · Cape viewpoint (anime pilgrimage)

    523 Kudeken, Chinen, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), ANIMETOURISM88, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  17. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Haebaru Army Hospital Shelter No. 20 (南風原陸軍病院壕 20号壕)

    Hand-dug tunnel used as a ward of the Okinawa Army Hospital in 1945, where the Himeyuri student nurses were first assigned before the retreat south. Guided visits by appointment through the Haebaru Town Culture Center (¥300).

    Look for WWII hospital tunnel (guided, by reservation)

    Kyan, Haebaru, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), showcaves.com (cave & subterranea reference), Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  18. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Cape Kyan & the Peace Tower, Itoman (喜屋武岬)

    The south-western tip of the main island, 10–20 m cliffs where the Pacific meets the East China Sea; this coast saw the last desperate fighting of the Battle of Okinawa, and the 1969 Peace Tower memorial stands at the point, inside Okinawa Senseki Quasi-National Park.

    Look for Southwest tip, war-memorial cliffs

    Kyan, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Itoman City — Itoman kankō navi (official)

  19. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Shimashi Ōzato Castle Ruins, Nanjō (島添大里城跡)

    A 14th-century gusuku on the eastern end of a ~150 m limestone ridge, seat of the Shimashi-Ōzato lords until Shō Hashi took it in 1402 on his way to unifying the Ryūkyū Kingdom; designated a National Historic Site in 2012.

    Look for Shō Hashi's first conquest

    Ōzato, Ōzato, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan (Ōzato Castle Ruins Park)

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Nanjotourism, Shirobito (城びと) — castle portal

  20. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Poké Lid — Wartortle & Sandygast, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (ポケふた カメール×スナバァ 道の駅いとまん)

    A Pokémon manhole cover showing Wartortle and Sandygast on an Itoman sandy beach. It is set inside the covered eating area of Michi-no-Eki Itoman, the roadside station that houses the fishermen's co-op fish market. It is one of three south-Okinawa lids unveiled together for Itoman, Tomigusuku and Nanjō, and is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Wartortle with Sandygast on Itoman's beach; the southern-Okinawa Poké Lid set (Itoman/Tomigusuku/Nanjō) · Pokémon manhole at the fish-market roadside station

    Michi-no-Eki Itoman (covered eating area), 4-19-1 Nishizaki-chō, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Ocvb, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  21. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Nanbu

    Inamine Hiyashimono Senmon Oshokujidokoro, Itoman (いなみね冷し物専門 お食事処)

    A long-running Itoman cold-sweets and set-meal shop (31 years per OCVB's Itoman listing) famous for its shirokuma — a mound of kintoki shaved ice decorated as a bear's face — alongside Okinawa soba and champurū set meals. Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā Aji Māi' column profiled the shirokuma, a house speciality for about 30 years, and Rurubu lists it as a signature Itoman sweets stop.

    1486-3 Itoman, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Ocvb, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  22. Worth the detour · Markets, Depachika & Street Food · Nanbu

    JA Farmers Market Itoman Umanchu Ichiba, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (ファーマーズマーケットいとまん うまんちゅ市場)

    Opened in November 2002 inside Michi-no-Eki Itoman, it is one of Okinawa's largest farm stands, with 1,000+ contracted growers and the highest footfall of the prefecture's ten JA farmers markets — Okinawa Times reported it passing 16 million visitors, and Ryukyu Shimpo covered its 10-millionth. OCVB's official Itoman gourmet course recommends its handmade onigiri, sweets and tropical fruit.

    Nishizaki-chō, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (inside Michi-no-Eki Itoman)

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Ocvb

  23. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Ryukyu Glass Village, Itoman (琉球ガラス村)

    Okinawa's largest handmade-glass factory, with galleries and shops of colourful Ryukyu glass and first-come glass-blowing classes at its Workshop Think Think. Rurubu lists it as a southern-Okinawa craft stop and Stripes Okinawa has covered its hands-on workshop.

    Look for Watch — and try — Ryukyu glass-blowing

    169 Fukuchi, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  24. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Ōjima Island (奥武島)

    Tiny bridge-linked fishing island off Nanjō, famous for cheap fresh-fish and seaweed tempura stands and its many cats.

    Look for Tempura island

    Ōjima, Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  25. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Valley of Gangala (ガンガラーの谷)

    Collapsed-cave valley of banyan-draped limestone opposite Okinawa World, where remains linked to the 18,000-year-old Minatogawa people were found; visits by guided tour only.

    Look for Guided cave-valley walk

    Maekawa, Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  26. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    DMM Kariyushi Aquarium (DMMかりゆし水族館)

    Okinawa's second-largest aquarium, in the iias Toyosaki mall near the airport: projection and AR-enhanced tanks, penguins, and a walkway over a big shark-and-ray tank.

    Look for Tech-forward aquarium

    iias Okinawa Toyosaki, Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  27. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Gushikawa Castle Ruins, Itoman (具志川城跡)

    Gusuku perched on sea cliffs at the southern tip of the island, surrounded by sea on three sides — a National Historic Site with sweeping coastal views.

    Look for Clifftop gusuku

    Kyan, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  28. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Itokazu Castle Ruins (糸数城跡)

    Fourteenth-century gusuku at 180 m — the highest castle ruin in the south — its curved limestone walls built to guard Tamagusuku; views over the southern coast.

    Look for Gusuku ruin

    Itokazu, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  29. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Tamagusuku Castle Ruins (玉城城跡)

    The oldest castle on Okinawa Island, said to have been built by the creator goddess Amamikiyo; its arched gate in the natural rock frames the solstice sunrise. National Historic Site.

    Look for Mythic gusuku

    Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Okinawa

  30. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Azama Sun Sun Beach (あざまサンサンビーチ)

    Shallow family beach by Azama port (the ferry to Kudaka), fringed with lawns, with a beach house and reservable BBQ sets.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — the beach's wooden swing appears in the series; Nanjō named an 'Anime Pilgrimage 88' site (Ryukyu Shimpo entry-1580769) · Family beach

    Azama, Chinen, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  31. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Mibaru Beach & glass-bottom boats (新原ビーチ)

    Two kilometres of natural sand on the south-east coast, launch point for glass-bottom boats over the reef.

    Look for Beach & glass-boat tours

    Hyakuna, Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  32. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Nirai Kanai Bridge overlook (ニライカナイ橋)

    A sweeping U-shaped road bridge that switchbacks down the Chinen hillside with the Pacific and Kudaka Island ahead — best seen from the tunnel-top viewpoint. It appears in the 2021 anime 'The Aquatope on White Sand', which earned Nanjō a place among the Anime Tourism Association's 88 anime pilgrimage sites.

    Your guide’s note ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — bridge shown in the series; Nanjō named an 'Anime Pilgrimage 88' site · Coastal bridge & viewpoint (anime pilgrimage)

    Chinen, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Govonline, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報)

  33. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Okinawa Karate Kaikan (沖縄空手会館)

    The prefecture's home of karate, opened March 2017 on a 3.8 ha site near Naha Airport: a museum on the art's Okinawan origins, training dojo and the ceremonial Shureikan hall.

    Look for Karate museum & dojo

    Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Japan Experience

  34. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Nanjō City Regional Products Hall — Midori no Yakata Sēfā (南城市地域物産館 緑の館・セーファ)

    The roadside products hall at the foot of Sēfa-utaki, with about 200 local souvenirs downstairs and a restaurant and café upstairs. It is the official Aquatope pilgrimage base: Nanjō keeps its Anime Tourism Association '88 Anime Pilgrimage' certification plate and goshuin-style memorial stamp here.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (2021) — holds Nanjō's Anime Tourism '88' certification plate and pilgrimage stamp · Aquatope pilgrimage stamp & plate

    539 Kudeken, Chinen, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), ANIMETOURISM88

  35. Worth the detour · Nanbu

    Konpaku-no-tō memorial, Itoman (魂魄の塔)

    The first war memorial raised after the Battle of Okinawa, built by residents themselves in February 1946 from gathered remains; enshrining some 35,000 people, it is the largest in the prefecture, and families gather here at dawn every Irei-no-hi (23 June).

    Look for First post-war memorial (1946)

    1441-3 Komesu, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Soumu, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報)

  36. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Nanbu

    Umibudō Farm Umin-chi, Itoman (海ぶどう農園 海ん道)

    A working sea-grape (umibudō) farm on the Itoman coast with a shop, its own Okinawa soba restaurant and picking experiences; its signature is soft serve folded with fresh-picked sea grapes. Ryukyu Shimpo reported on the farm and OCVB's official Itoman–Tomigusuku 'fishermen's-town gourmet' course includes it as a stop.

    1931 Maesato, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Ocvb

  37. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Nanbu

    Hamabe no Chaya (浜辺の茶屋)

    Founded in 1994 as Okinawa's first seaside café: a driftwood lodge on a shallow beach whose window counter sits right over the water at high tide.

    2-1 Tamagusuku, Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  38. Worth the detour · Tofu, Shōjin & Vegetarian · Nanbu

    Kaiyō Shokudō, Tomigusuku (海洋食堂)

    Tomigusuku shokudō famous for yushi-dōfu, soft just-made island tofu carried over from the adjoining tofu works and served in soup or soba.

    Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawatraveler, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  39. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Nanbu

    Awamori Masahiro Gallery, Itoman (泡盛まさひろギャラリー)

    Gallery-shop of Masahiro Distillery (founded 1883): watch the production line through glass, browse displays on awamori's history and taste for free.

    5-8-7 Nishizaki-chō, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler

  40. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Nanbu

    Mozuku Soba Kunnatu, Nanjō (もずくそばの店 くんなとぅ)

    Facing Ōjima, a mozuku-farming centre, this shop kneads JAS-organic mozuku into its own soba noodles and serves them in a light bonito broth with tempura fried to order.

    460-2 Shikenbaru, Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  41. Worth the detour · Tempura, Tonkatsu & Agemono · Nanbu

    Ōshiro Tempura, Ōjima (大城てんぷら店)

    One of the three tempura stands on 'tempura island' Ōjima, under shade trees right by the water; fish, vegetable and squid tempura are fried after you order, for a few coins apiece.

    193 Tamagusuku Ōjima, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  42. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Nanbu

    Taco Rice Café Kijimunā, Senaga-jima Umikaji Terrace (タコライスcafe きじむなぁ 瀬長島ウミカジテラス店)

    The Umikaji Terrace branch of Kijimunā, the shop that created 'omu-taco' (taco rice under a soft omelette) in Onna in 2003 and has since won awards at Okinawa gourmet festivals. Rurubu picks it among Umikaji Terrace's recommended eats and Okinawa Traveler includes it in its seven popular taco-rice shops.

    174-6 Senaga, Tomigusuku, Okinawa 901-0233, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler

  43. Deep cut · Nanbu

    Poké Lid — Axew & Jangmo-o on a Hārī boat, Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki (ポケふた キバゴ×ジャラコ 道の駅豊崎)

    Tomigusuku's Pokémon manhole cover shows Axew and Jangmo-o riding a dragon boat, a nod to the city's claim to be the birthplace of the Hārī boat race. It sits at Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki, the roadside station near Naha Airport. It was installed in the same south-Okinawa set as the Itoman and Nanjō lids, and is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Axew & Jangmo-o on a Hārī dragon boat, Tomigusuku's lid in the southern-Okinawa set · Pokémon manhole near the airport

    Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki, 3-39 Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Ocvb, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  44. Deep cut · Nanbu

    Chinen Castle Ruins (知念城跡)

    Compact cliff-top gusuku with a pair of arched stone gates, believed to be the second-oldest castle in the Ryūkyūs; near the sacred Chinen-Ukka spring. National Historic Site.

    Look for Gusuku ruin

    Chinen, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  45. Deep cut · Nanbu

    Toyosaki Chura-Sun Beach (豊崎美らSUNビーチ)

    Long artificial beach on the Toyosaki reclamation near the airport, with BBQ areas and planes overhead.

    Look for Beach near the airport

    Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  46. Deep cut · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Nanbu

    Do~me Gohan Café, Ryukyu Glass Village, Itoman (土～夢ごはんカフェ)

    The café beside the glass-blowing workshop at Ryukyu Glass Village, serving meat and fish mains — notably butter-soy gurukun, Okinawa's prefectural fish — with island-vegetable side dishes on local pottery and Ryukyu glass. JAL's Skyward crew picks recommend it and Stripes Okinawa reviewed it.

    169 Fukuchi, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (Ryukyu Glass Village)

    Recommended by Jal Skyward+ (jal in-flight magazine web), Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  47. Deep cut · Kissaten & Coffee · Nanbu

    Café Kurukuma (カフェくるくま)

    Cliff-top Asian-herb restaurant café with a terrace and herb-garden promenade looking out over the Pacific.

    1190 Chinen, Chinen, Nanjō, Okinawa 901-1513, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  48. Deep cut · Markets, Depachika & Street Food · Nanbu

    Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki (道の駅 豊崎)

    The roadside station closest to Naha Airport, stocked with Tomigusuku's mango products and island produce — a last-stop for food souvenirs.

    Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawatraveler

  49. Deep cut · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Nanbu

    Uema Kashiten Factory — Suppaiman (上間菓子店 工場見学)

    Free factory tour of the maker of Suppaiman, Okinawa's cult dried-plum snack and its mascot; watch the plums and candies being made (video only on Saturdays).

    3-64 Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawatraveler

  50. Deep cut · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Nanbu

    Minatomachi Parlor, Itoman (港町パーラー)

    A small counter opened in April 2025 inside Itoman's public market 'Itomāru' by the second-generation head of Kinshiro Sengyo, a fish shop trading in Itoman for 35+ years; the owner fillets the day's catch on the spot for generous local-fish bowls. Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā Ajimāi' series and OTV Okitive both featured it.

    989-83 Itoman, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (Itoman Market Itomāru)

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive

  51. Deep cut · International & Fusion · Nanbu

    Hawaiian Pancake Cafe KOA, Itoman (Hawaiian Pancake Cafe KOA)

    A beachfront Hawaiian café in Itoman that the Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā Ajimāi' column (no. 144) calls stylish and generous. Stars and Stripes Okinawa recommends its hearty loco moco and pancakes, with an ocean view, as a refuel stop on a southern-Okinawa drive.

    Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (beachfront; Stars and Stripes GPS N26.117810 E127.662568 — street number not captured)

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  52. Deep cut · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Nanbu

    Oyaji no Maguro, Senaga-jima Umikaji Terrace (親父のまぐろ)

    A tuna-bowl counter at Umikaji Terrace where a fisherman father line-catches the tuna and his son and daughter-in-law serve it fresh and never frozen. It is known for thick-cut yellowfin maguro-don and an ahi poke rice. Rurubu lists it among the terrace's recommended eats and the Ryukyu Shimpo has profiled it.

    Senaga-jima Umikaji Terrace, 174-6 Senaga, Tomigusuku, Okinawa 901-0233, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報)

Hokubu 78

Northern Okinawa (Nago · Motobu & Churaumi · Kouri Island · Onna · Yanbaru

  1. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Kishimoto Shokudo (きしもと食堂)

    Soba shop founded in 1905 near the Motobu market: flat noodles still made with tree-ash lye water, in a light bonito-and-soy broth with thick boneless rib, kamaboko and island onion.

    near Motobu Municipal Market, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Ramen Adventures (Brian MacDuckston), Okinawa Times

  2. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    King Tacos Kin (キングタコス 金武本店)

    The taco-rice institution in downtown Kin: seasoned taco meat, cheese, lettuce and tomato over rice — the dish created in Kin in 1984 by Matsuzo Gibo of Parlor Senri.

    Kin, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Explore Parts Unknown (CNN / Anthony Bourdain), Japan Travel (japantravel.com)

  3. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Gabusoka Shokudo Honten (我部祖河食堂 本店)

    Founded in 1966 and billed as the birthplace of soki soba: the founder, then a butcher, simmered unsold spare ribs for hours and laid them on soba. House-made wavy noodles, punchy pork-bone broth.

    Gabusoka, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawa Times

  4. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Yanbaru Soba (山原そば)

    The queue-before-opening star of the Motobu 'soba road' (Route 84): a mellow bonito-and-pork broth unchanged for four decades, soki or three-layer pork on top; closes when the noodles run out.

    70-1 Izumi, Motobu, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawa Times

  5. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Ufuya (百年古家 大家)

    A century-old Okinawan farmhouse compound in the hills above Nago serving soki soba and agu pork; one of Okinawa Traveler's locals-recommend five and on Stars and Stripes' soba trail.

    Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Okinawatraveler, Okinawa Prefecture — 「琉球料理が味わえる店」 certification

  6. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Hokubu

    Arakaki Zenzai-ya (新垣ぜんざい屋)

    Motobu's half-century-old zenzai shop that does exactly one thing: sweet stewed red kidney beans buried under a peak of shaved ice, bought with a ticket from the door.

    11-2 Toguchi, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawatraveler, Gigazine, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  7. Must see · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Hokubu

    Orion Happy Park — Orion Beer Nago Brewery (オリオンハッピーパーク)

    Okinawa's own beer since 1957: the Nago plant's tour ends with a tasting of just-brewed Orion Draft; shop, restaurant and a small history gallery.

    Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Okinawatraveler

  8. Must see · Markets, Depachika & Street Food · Hokubu

    Onna no Eki Nakayukui Ichiba (おんなの駅 なかゆくい市場)

    West-coast roadside market that every drive north stops at: island produce, snack stalls frying sata andagi (brown sugar, beni-imo and more), and Ryu-pin's mountainous tropical-fruit kakigōri.

    Nakadomari, Onna, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  9. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Emi no Mise, Ōgimi (笑味の店)

    Opened in 1990 by Kinjō Shōko to pass on the food culture of Ōgimi, the 'longevity village'; a farm restaurant whose reservation-only chōju-zen longevity set is built on seasonal island vegetables she grows herself. Her book of Yanbaru grandmothers' kitchen wisdom was published in 2023 (Ryukyu Shimpo).

    61 Ōganeku, Ōgimi-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Okinawa Prefecture — 「琉球料理が味わえる店」 certification

  10. Must see · Hokubu

    Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium (沖縄美ら海水族館)

    Widely rated Japan's best aquarium, at the tip of the Motobu Peninsula. Its Kuroshio Tank — one of the largest in the world — holds whale sharks and manta rays.

    Look for Whale-shark aquarium

    Ocean Expo Park, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Visit Okinawa

  11. Must see · Hokubu

    Cape Manzamo (万座毛)

    Grassy clifftop above the Onna coast with the elephant-trunk rock arch; one of the island's most-visited viewpoints.

    Look for Clifftop viewpoint

    Onna, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  12. Must see · Hokubu

    Hiji Falls (比地大滝)

    The main island's tallest waterfall (25.7 m), reached by a forest trail and suspension bridge through the Yanbaru subtropical woods from the Kunigami campground.

    Look for Yanbaru waterfall hike

    Kunigami Forest Park, Hiji, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  13. Must see · Hokubu

    Cape Hedo (辺戸岬)

    The northernmost point of Okinawa Island: jagged limestone cliffs where the East China Sea meets the Pacific, with Yoron Island on the horizon and the Yanbaru-kuina observatory on the hill behind.

    Look for Northern cape

    Hedo, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  14. Must see · Hokubu

    Cape Maeda & the Blue Cave (真栄田岬 青の洞窟)

    Limestone cape on the Onna coast and the island's most popular snorkel and dive entry; swim or boat into the Blue Cave, where light through the sea floor turns the grotto luminous aquamarine.

    Look for Snorkel cave

    Maeda, Onna, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  15. Must see · Hokubu

    Kouri Ōhashi Bridge & Kouri Island (古宇利大橋・古宇利島)

    The 1,960 m toll-free bridge (2005) from Yagaji Island across emerald shallows to Kouri, the 'Island of Love' — one of Okinawa's signature drives, with beaches, Heart Rock and garlic-shrimp trucks at the far end.

    Look for Sea bridge & island

    Kouri, Nakijin, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Ocvb

  16. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Shinzan Soba (新山そば)

    Nago soba house founded in 1925 and run by the third generation: thick, springy flat noodles in an agu-pork-bone and bonito broth; profiled by the Okinawa Times as a century-old favourite.

    1-9-2 Daito, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawa Times

  17. Must see · Kissaten & Coffee · Hokubu

    Pizza Kissa Kajinhō, Motobu (ピザ喫茶 花人逢)

    Red-tiled old-house café on a hilltop above Motobu serving the same home-made pizza for a quarter-century; on clear days Ie-jima, Sesoko and Minna float on the horizon.

    1153-2 Yamazato, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler

  18. Must see · Soba & Udon · Hokubu

    Maeda Shokudō, Ōgimi (前田食堂)

    Yanbaru noodle shop founded in 1972, on the way to Hiji Falls and Mt Yonaha; its signature gyūniku soba piles pepper-fried beef and bean sprouts on thin noodles, and weekend queues are the norm. Closes when the broth runs out.

    Tsuha, Ōgimi, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Okinawatraveler

  19. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Shima-buta Shichirin-yaki Manmi, Nago (島豚七輪焼 満味)

    Reservation-essential grill house for Yanbaru island pork descended from agu: cuts and offal grilled over individual charcoal shichirin, with rare pork tongue and a horumon fried rice to finish. Dinner only (closed Sun–Mon).

    251 Isagawa, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  20. Must see · International & Fusion · Hokubu

    Seaside Drive-In, Onna (シーサイドドライブイン)

    Opened in 1967 under US administration and kept in its original style, neon signs and all; the signature creamy pork-bone soup is a take-out ritual for west-coast beach days, and a 24-hour take-out counter sells burgers, shaved ice and sides.

    Nakadomari, Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (Route 58, seaside)

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  21. Must see · Soba & Udon · Hokubu

    Sawanoya Motobu Honten (さわのや 本部本店)

    One of the anchors of the 'Motobu Soba Kaidō' noodle road: noodles are hand-made the old way with wood-ash lye, giving firm, flat thick noodles with a distinctive flavour (Mapple); Stars and Stripes Okinawa features it in its guide to slurping noodles like a local.

    Motobu-chō (Motobu Soba Kaidō, Prefectural Route 84), Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  22. Must see · Hokubu

    Nakijin Castle Ruins (今帰仁城跡)

    Hilltop stronghold of the Hokuzan kingdom with long serpentine limestone walls. UNESCO Gusuku component.

    Look for Gusuku ruins

    Nakijin, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO

  23. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Michi-no-Eki Ginoza (道の駅ぎのざ)

    A roadside station on Route 329, the first on Okinawa's east coast. It is known for its water-play plaza and giant slide, and an All About 2025 survey ranked it second among Okinawa roadside stations to visit with children. One of the three official Okitsura manhole covers, showing the heroines and Ginoza's mascot Gī-no-kun, was installed here as part of the Kin Bay council's pilgrimage campaign.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Okitsura (沖縄で好きになった子が方言すぎてツラすぎる, anime 2025) — official Okitsura manhole (with Ginoza mascot Gī-no-kun) · Okitsura manhole at a family roadside station

    1633 Kanna, Ginoza Village, Kunigami District, Okinawa 904-1304, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Kintown, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), All About (allabout.co.jp), Ginoza Village official site (宜野座村)

  24. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Hokubu

    Captain Kangaroo, Nago (キャプテンカンガルー)

    A burger shop that began as an Osaka bar in 1999 and opened in Nago in 2007, moving to its current Umusa site in 2020. Stars and Stripes Okinawa calls it a hot spot for its taco rice as well as its burgers; OTV Okitive profiles its Mexican-loaded 'Captain Kangaroo taco rice', and Smart Magazine ranks it among Okinawa's top one or two burger shops.

    183 Umusa, Nago-shi, Okinawa 905-0006, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Smartmagazine, Ocvb, Tabirai

  25. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    KIN Sunrise Beach (KINサンライズビーチ海浜公園)

    An 800 m long-beach seaside park in Kin, listed by the OCVB film office as a location. It is one of the three official pilgrimage stops for the manga and anime 'Okitsura': one of the series' manhole covers was installed here, and the Kin Bay council ran its Okitsura collaboration campaign from the park's management building. The campaign art shows the heroines eating taco rice, the dish that started in Kin, against this beach.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Okitsura (沖縄で好きになった子が方言すぎてツラすぎる, anime 2025) — official Okitsura manhole + Kan-Kin-Bay council collab campaign site · Okitsura manhole & collab beach

    10819-4 Kin, Kin Town, Kunigami District, Okinawa 904-1201, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Kintown, Ocvb, Kin Sunrise Beach official site

  26. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    JUNGLIA Okinawa theme park, Nakijin/Nago (ジャングリア沖縄)

    A 60-hectare nature theme park on a former golf course straddling Nakijin and Nago at the edge of Yanbaru, opened 25 July 2025 by Katana Inc. (led by ex-USJ marketer Tsuyoshi Morioka): animatronic-dinosaur rides, buggy safaris, bungee and an aerial course, plus a spa annex and 15 restaurants (Stars and Stripes; The Japan Times; nippon.com/Jiji).

    Your guide’s note Northern Okinawa's new jungle theme park (opened July 2025)

    553-1 Gogayama, Nakijin-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa 905-0413, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, The Japan Times, nippon.com (Nippon Communications Foundation), Tabirai

  27. Worth the detour · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Hokubu

    Nago Fishing Port Fish Market & Diner (名護漁港水産物直販所)

    A fish-sales hall with an attached diner inside Nago fishing port on Route 58, cooking fish auctioned that day at the port. Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā aji māi' column praised its seafood bowl of many fish, Okinawa Times' driver-lunch column went for the squid-ink soup and tempura, and the Nago tourism association lists it.

    3-5-16 Gusuku, Nago-shi, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Okinawa Times, Tabirai, Nagokanko

  28. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Hokubu

    Ōgimi Shīkwāsā Park (大宜味シークヮーサーパーク)

    Billed by the OCVB as Okinawa's first shīkwāsā theme park, in the citrus's home village of Ōgimi: a free-entry factory where you watch the pressing line, compare juices from each month's harvest and eat in a restaurant cooking with shīkwāsā powder. Ryukyu Shimpo covered its completion as a local-produce revitalisation project; the Yanbaru three-villages tourism portal lists it.

    1424-1 Tsuha, Ōgimi-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa 905-1318, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), YAMBARU3KANKO, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  29. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Hokubu

    Famille tacos, Nago (Famille)

    A takeout taco stand opened in July 2025 on the national road to Junglia by a couple who cooked in French hotel restaurants; the meat takes three days to develop its flavour. Covered by Okinawa Times and Ryukyu Shimpo, and ranked No. 2 in the north in OTV Okitive's 2026 Golden Week 30, which says its 200 tacos a day sell out.

    35 Yabe, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Ocvb, Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive

  30. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Hokubu

    Hammock Garden Anettai Chaya, Motobu (亜熱帯茶屋)

    An Asian-style hillside café opened in May 2015 up a single-lane lane in Motobu, near Churaumi, with hammocks, arbours and mostly outdoor seats looking over forest and sea. Stars and Stripes Okinawa reviewed it for its food and coastal view; the OCVB, Mapple and Tabirai list its brunch toasts and Yanbaru-herb chicken gapao rice.

    60 Nohara, Motobu-cho, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Ocvb, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Tabirai

  31. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Hokubu

    CASA SOL, Nakijin (カーサソル)

    A forest-hill café over the Haneji inland sea opened on 17 September 2024 by a YouTuber couple, built from glass-walled containers with a driftwood 'bird's nest' lookout and a giant swing (OTV Okitive, Tabirai). Its menu draws on the owners' world travels — açai bowls made without frozen fruit, poke bowls, smoothies and morning plates; rurubu ranks it among Okinawa's six best Yanbaru forest cafés.

    661 Wakugawa, Nakijin-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa 905-0412, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Tabirai, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), OKINAWA41

  32. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Neo Park Okinawa, Nago (ネオパークオキナワ)

    Nago's municipal wildlife and botanical park (opened December 1992): about 100 species in free-roaming Africa, Amazon and Oceania zones, circled by a small light railway.

    Look for Walk-through flamingo & bird park

    4607-41 Nago, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Wikipedia JA, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  33. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Kayauchi Banta cliff, Kunigami (茅打バンタ)

    A ~100 m sheer cliff and lookout near the island's northern tip, inside Yanbaru National Park; the name ('banta' = cliff) comes from the tale that a bundle of thatch thrown over the edge was torn apart by the wind.

    Look for Yanbaru's 100 m cliff lookout

    Ginama, Kunigami-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Jta Tagengo, Ocvb

  34. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Busena Marine Park Underwater Observatory, Nago (ブセナ海中公園 海中展望塔)

    Opened in 1970 at the tip of Busena Cape, the observatory stands 170 m offshore at the end of a footbridge; a spiral stair descends to round windows 5 m below the surface for watching reef fish. Glass-bottom boats run from the same park.

    Look for Walk down to the reef 5 m underwater

    1744-1 Kise, Nago-shi, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler

  35. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Ryukyu Mura, Onna (琉球村)

    A hands-on culture village of old Okinawan farmhouses moved here from around the islands, recreating pre-war village life; visitors try indigo dyeing, pottery, weaving and bingata stencil-dyeing and watch Ryukyuan performing-arts shows.

    Look for Old Okinawa's relocated farmhouses

    1130 Yamada, Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa 904-0416, Japan

    Recommended by Onna Village — ココイコ！恩納村 (official tourism pages), KNT, Official Site

  36. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Poké Lid — Emolga & Pikipek at Hinpun Gajumaru, Nago (ポケふた エモンガ×ツツケラ ひんぷんガジュマル)

    A Pokémon manhole cover (Poké Lid) set beside Nago's Hinpun Gajumaru, the 240-plus-year-old national-monument banyan on Nago's main street. It shows Emolga and Pikipek playing in the tree. Nago installed it in Gajumaru Ryokuchi Park on 15 February 2022, and it is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Emolga & Pikipek playing in the Hinpun Gajumaru, Nago's symbol; northern stop on the Okinawa Poké Lid trail · Pokémon manhole under Nago's great banyan

    Gajumaru Ryokuchi Park, 2-321-3 Gusuku, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Ocvb

  37. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Yanbaru Kuina Ecological Exhibit 'Kuina no Mori', Kunigami (ヤンバルクイナ生態展示学習施設 クイナの森)

    The place to actually see the Okinawa rail (Yanbaru kuina), the flightless national natural monument found only in Yanbaru: a live exhibit and learning facility in Ada village, part of the Ada Kuina Fureai Park. The OCVB features it in its ethical-travel series on learning about Yanbaru nature; Mapple lists it (9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30).

    Look for Meet the flightless Okinawa rail

    1477-35 Ada, Kunigami-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Official Site

  38. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Hokubu

    Bookcafe Okinawa Rail, Kunigami (ブックカフェ オキナワレイル)

    An off-grid concrete book café on the forest road toward Yonaha-dake inside Yanbaru National Park, named for the Yanbaru kuina (Okinawa rail), running on solar power and spring water with walls of books. Ryukyu Shimpo covered its opening as a forest reading retreat; OTV Okitive calls it worth the trip, and Tabirai recommends the New York cheesecake and house-roasted coffee.

    2040-107 Ōho-shagahara, Okuma, Kunigami-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Tabirai

  39. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Nakamura Soba (なかむらそば)

    Roadside soba house near Manza Beach: preservative-free house noodles, a light but bonito-rich broth and pork belly that falls apart at a touch; the aasa soba works sea lettuce into both noodles and topping.

    1669-1 Serakaki, Onna, Okinawa 904-0404, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Okinawatraveler, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  40. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Hokubu

    Helios Distillery (ヘリオス酒造)

    Founded as a rum distiller in 1961 and brewing Okinawa's pioneering craft beer since 1996; the free tour shows 2,600 barrels of aging awamori stacked to the roof.

    405 Kyoda, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Beer Tengoku (ビール天国), Okinawatraveler

  41. Worth the detour · Markets, Depachika & Street Food · Hokubu

    Michi-no-Eki Kyoda — Yanbaru Bussan Center (道の駅許田)

    The roadside station at the end of the Okinawa Expressway, gateway to Yanbaru: produce from the twelve northern towns and a takeout row famous for hot Okinawan tempura and tacos. Renewed in 2021.

    17-1 Kyoda, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawatraveler

  42. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Hokubu

    Cafe ichara, Motobu (カフェ イチャラ)

    A Motobu forest café picked by Rurubu, Mapple and Okinawa Traveler's 'sea or forest?' round-up of northern cafés.

    Izumi, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawatraveler

  43. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Hokubu

    Okashi Goten Onna (御菓子御殿 恩納店)

    The red-gated seaside flagship of the confectioner behind the 'original' beni-imo tart, made from 100% Okinawan purple sweet potato from contracted farmers with no preservatives or colouring; the baking line is visible through glass and a reservation-only tart-making class runs here.

    Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (coastal Route 58; red-gated palace-style shop)
