  44. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Hokubu

    Iejima Distillery, Ie Island (伊江島蒸留所)

    The island's rum distillery, set up in a former bioethanol demonstration plant, makes Ie Rum Santa Maria as agricole rum from local sugarcane juice. It won Best Japanese Rum of the Year at the first Tokyo Whiskey & Spirits Competition in 2019. A distillery-limited bottling took a top gold medal in the 2026 edition. The island is a 30-minute ferry ride from Motobu Port.

    1627-3 Higashi-Ebusaki, Ie-son, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  45. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Hokubu

    Nakijin Soba (今帰仁そば)

    An Okinawa soba shop in an old Ryūkyū house in a fukugi-lined village near Churaumi, known for its light but rich broth and melting nankotsu sōki. When it faced closure, fans of the shop took it over; it reopened renewed in its 10th year with outdoor seating (Okinawa Times), and ran a limited Naha pop-up in 2026.

    181 Moroshi, Nakijin-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Okinawa Times

  46. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Hokubu

    CAFE FUKURUBI, Kouri Island (カフェ フクルビ)

    A café-restaurant on high ground near Heart Rock on Kouri Island's north side, with a 180-degree panorama of the horizon from its terrace. It cooks with prefectural ingredients and especially Kouri Island's own pure brown sugar, used in its signature black-sugar French toast.

    2516 Kouri, Nakijin-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawaclip, Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Nakijinkanko

  47. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Minna Island — 'Croissant Island', Motobu (水納島)

    A small crescent-shaped coral island (0.47 km², highest point 26.9 m) off the Motobu Peninsula, nicknamed 'Croissant Island' because it looks like one from the air. The OCVB lists it and its Minna Beach as a day-trip swimming and snorkelling spot.

    Look for The croissant-shaped coral island off Motobu

    Minna-jima, Motobu-cho, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wiki, Ocvb

  48. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Kin Kannon-ji Temple, Kin (金武観音寺)

    A Kōyasan Shingon temple (mountain name Kinpusan, main image Shō-Kannon) traditionally founded in the 16th century by the monk Nisshū, who was shipwrecked at Kin while sailing from Kii and preached from the limestone cave beside the temple. Kin town's tourism site lists the cave (Nisshū-dō) and the temple's old fukugi trees.

    Look for 16th-century temple over the Kin limestone cave

    222 Kin, Kin-chō, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wiki, Kintown, Kintown

  49. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Tokei Beach & Heart Rock, Kouri Island (ティーヌ浜)

    The north-shore cove of 'Love Island' Kouri, reached by the long Kouri Ōhashi bridge, where the heart-shaped rock formation stands in the shallows.

    Look for Heart Rock beach

    Kouri, Nakijin, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  50. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    ASMUI Spiritual Hikes (former Daisekirinzan, 大石林山)

    Trails through jagged limestone karst near Cape Hedo, a place of prayer for some 600 years — renamed ASMUI Spiritual Hikes.

    Look for Karst trails

    Ginama, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  51. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Bise Fukugi Tree Road (備瀬のフクギ並木)

    Kilometre of sandy lanes in Bise village tunnelled by centuries-old fukugi windbreak trees, five minutes from Churaumi; walk or cycle to Cape Bise.

    Look for Fukugi-tree village lanes

    Bise, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Atlas Obscura

  52. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Nago Central Park / Nago Castle Park (名護城公園)

    Hillside park on the old Nago gusuku site — the only place in Okinawa on Japan's list of 100 best cherry-blossom spots (deep-pink kanhi-zakura in late January) — with the Tenjo lookout over Nago Bay.

    Look for January cherry-blossom park

    Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  53. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Ie Island & Mt Gusuku 'Tatchu' (伊江島 城山)

    Flat island a 30-minute ferry from Motobu, dominated by the 172 m rock spire of Gusuku-yama ('Iejima Tatchu') — climb for views back to the Motobu Peninsula.

    Look for Island & rock-spire climb

    Ie, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  54. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Sesoko Island & Sesoko Beach (瀬底島)

    Small bridged island off Motobu with one of the main island area's clearest swimming beaches, facing Minna and Ie islands.

    Look for Bridged island beach

    Sesoko, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  55. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Mt Yaedake cherry-blossom road (八重岳桜の森公園)

    Japan's first cherry blossoms of the year: about 7,000 deep-pink kanhi-zakura line a 4 km road up the main island's second-highest mountain, with a festival from mid-January.

    Look for January sakura road

    Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Japan-guide

  56. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Emerald Beach, Ocean Expo Park (エメラルドビーチ)

    Three-part beach inside Ocean Expo Park beside Churaumi, one of Japan's '100 best beaches'; free entry and parking, swimming April–October.

    Look for Beach

    Ocean Expo Park, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Japan-guide

  57. Worth the detour · Hokubu

    Gesashi Bay mangroves, Higashi (慶佐次湾のヒルギ林)

    The second-largest mangrove forest on Okinawa's main island — about 10 ha along the Gesashi River estuary, explored by boardwalk or guided kayak.

    Look for Mangrove kayaking

    Gesashi, Higashi, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Wikipedia JA

  58. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Izumi Soba (伊豆味そば)

    Soba stop on the Route 84 'soba road' through Izumi, picked in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers as one of the north's best.

    Izumi, Motobu, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  59. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Sobaya Yoshiko, Motobu (そば屋よしこ)

    One of the stars of Motobu's 'soba highway' (Prefectural Route 84, 20-plus soba shops): come for the meltingly braised tebichi on a pork-bonito-kombu broth.

    Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawatraveler

  60. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Hokubu

    Yachimun Kissa Shīsā-en, Motobu (やちむん喫茶 シーサー園)

    A red-roofed Okinawan farmhouse swallowed by subtropical forest, with more than a hundred local potters' shīsā lions perched on roofs and walls around the tables.

    1439 Izumi, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  61. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Okinawa Ryōri Maruoki Shōten, Nago (沖縄料理 丸沖商店)

    Nago restaurant certified under Okinawa Prefecture's 'shop where you can taste Ryūkyū cuisine' scheme; known for its agu-pork shabu-shabu course.

    Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Prefecture — 「琉球料理が味わえる店」 certification, Okinawatraveler

  62. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Hokubu

    Yae Shokudō, Nago (八重食堂)

    A 40-plus-year-old Nago soba shop known for topping up bowls with broth from a kettle (OCVB); voted into Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle fans for the best soba in the north.

    1-9-3 Gusuku, Nago-shi, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Ocvb

  63. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Hokubu

    Sakihama Seimen, Onna (崎濱製麺)

    Reopened in Yamada in April 2024 as the rebrand of a Tomari (Naha) soba shop that ran 8 years; noodles are rested 3+ days and ordered kufa (hard), regular or yafa (soft), in a clear pork-bonito-kelp shio broth with no pork bones (OTV okitive). OCVB's soba-lovers' picks feature it.

    847 Yamada, Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa 904-0416, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Ocvb

  64. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Hokubu

    Yaezen, Motobu (八重善)

    A soba stop on Motobu's Route 84 'soba road', named by the OCVB soba-road itinerary for its signature bowl that combines Okinawa soba with squid-ink broth made with fresh local white squid. rurubu lists the ikasumi soba as limited to 10 servings a day, plus sōki soba and the seasonal 'Yaezen gozen' set.

    342-1 Namizato, Motobu-cho, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  65. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Hokubu

    Marutaka Soba, Nago (丸隆そば)

    A Nago soba house founded in 1948 (formerly Ganaha Soba) that OTV Okitive presents as a 70-plus-year institution serving the 'original' sōki soba — flat wide noodles in a bonito-forward broth. Listed by the Nago City tourism association.

    1-10-25 Ōkita, Nago-shi, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Nagokanko

  66. Deep cut · Hokubu

    Kouri Ocean Tower, Kouri Island (古宇利オーシャンタワー)

    A white observation tower on Kouri Island whose deck stands 82 m above sea level, looking over the cobalt sea and the Kouri Ōhashi bridge; Okinawa Traveler's northern-cafés feature recommends a meal there with the view. Listed by the OCVB and the Nakijin Village tourism association.

    Look for 82 m above the sea, looking down the Kouri bridge

    538 Kouri, Nakijin-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Nakijinkanko, Okinawatraveler, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  67. Deep cut · Hokubu

    Fukuji Dam & Lake Fukujō, Higashi (福地ダム・福上湖)

    Completed in 1974 on the Fukuji River, Okinawa's largest dam holds the prefecture's biggest reservoir, Lake Fukujō, chosen in 2005 as one of Japan's 100 best dam lakes. The Yanbaru three-villages tourism portal lists its lookouts, lakeside paths and water-resources exhibit hall, with nature-watching boat and canoe trips on the lake.

    Look for Okinawa's largest dam lake in the Yanbaru forest

    Fukuji River, Higashi-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wiki, YAMBARU3KANKO, Ocvb

  68. Deep cut · Hokubu

    OKINAWA Fruits Land, Nago (OKINAWAフルーツらんど)

    A tropical theme park in Nago on the road to Churaumi, where you walk among tropical and subtropical fruit trees and colourful southern birds and taste the fruit; listed by the OCVB and described on Japanese Wikipedia (open daily 10:00–17:30).

    Look for Tropical fruit trees and birds, then the tasting

    1220-71 Bimata, Nago-shi, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Wiki, Official Site

  69. Deep cut · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Hokubu

    Ryūkyū Ryōri Nago-magari Restaurant, Nago (名護曲レストラン)

    A long-running Ryukyu-cuisine restaurant on the coast road at Yofuke in Nago, listed by rurubu, Okinawa Traveler and the OCVB; rurubu notes the owner builds menus from rare and nutritious seasonal ingredients. The wide menu runs from Okinawan set meals and soba to Western dishes like taco rice and steak.

    574 Yofuke, Nago, Okinawa 905-0022, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler, Ocvb

  70. Deep cut · Hokubu

    Nago Pineapple Park (ナゴパイナップルパーク)

    Kitsch pineapple-themed park on Route 84 with self-driving pineapple carts through the plantation and tastings of pineapple everything.

    Look for Pineapple theme park

    Biimata, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  71. Deep cut · Hokubu

    Kariyushi Beach (かりゆしビーチ)

    Resort beach on Nago Bay's western shore with a long swimming season (March–October) and marine activities.

    Look for Resort beach

    Kise, Onna, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  72. Deep cut · Hokubu

    Okuma Beach (奥間ビーチ)

    Year-round beach resort in Yanbaru, inside the World Natural Heritage north; long a favourite of base families.

    Look for Yanbaru beach

    Okuma, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  73. Deep cut · Hokubu

    Todoroki Falls Park, Nago (轟の滝)

    A roughly 28 m waterfall a five-minute drive inland from Route 58, designated a prefectural scenic spot; a small managed park (open 9–18, ¥200) with stream play and barbecue areas.

    Look for Nago's 28 m forest falls

    594 Sukuta, Nago, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Ocvb

  74. Deep cut · International & Fusion · Hokubu

    GATE1, Kin (ゲート1)

    A retro-American diner facing Camp Hansen's Gate 1 in Kin, the birthplace of taco rice; Kin town's tourism site lists its big cheese-and-vegetable taco rice, jumbo burger and fried chicken, and notes it takes US dollars as well as yen. Stars and Stripes Okinawa names Gate 1, with King Tacos, as a long-running taco-rice favourite in Kin.

    4257 Kin, Kin-chō, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Kintown, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  75. Deep cut · Markets, Depachika & Street Food · Hokubu

    Michi-no-Eki Yuiyui Kunigami (道の駅 ゆいゆい国頭)

    The Yanbaru roadside station that gathers Kunigami village's food: Oku-grown green tea, karagi tea and the local Kunigami doughnuts — the last big food stop before Cape Hedo.

    Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawatraveler

  76. Deep cut · International & Fusion · Hokubu

    KOURI SHRIMP, Kouri Island (古宇利島 KOURI SHRIMP)

    Kouri Island's garlic-shrimp stand serving Hawaiian-style shrimp plates; Stars and Stripes notes it has opened a new shop on the island.

    314 Kouri, Nakijin, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  77. Deep cut · Kissaten & Coffee · Hokubu

    Cafe Hakoniwa, Motobu (Cafe ハコニワ)

    A 50-plus-year-old house in the Izumi hills, turned into a café with antique furniture. The signature is the Hakoniwa plate, home-style rice and side dishes made with locally grown vegetables. There are also cakes and shīkwāsā juice. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

    2566 Izumi, Motobu-chō, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawatraveler

  78. Deep cut · Kissaten & Coffee · Hokubu

    Cafe Kokuu, Nakijin (カフェこくう)

    A hilltop café in Nakijin whose cooking draws on Japanese and macrobiotic food. The signature Kokuu plate serves more than ten kinds of organically grown island vegetables, each cooked a different way, on yachimun pottery. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

    2031-138 Moroshi, Nakijin-son, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawatraveler, Savor Japan

Kerama & nearby islands 19

Tokashiki · Zamami · Aka · Kume-jima · Iheya

  1. Must see · Kerama & nearby islands

    Hate-no-hama sandbar, Kume Island (ハテの浜)

    A 7 km ribbon of pure white sand bars in the open sea east of Kume Island, reached only by a 20-minute boat ride — no shade, no buildings, just reef and sky.

    Look for Offshore sandbar

    off eastern Kume Island, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  2. Must see · Kerama & nearby islands

    Uegusuku Castle Ruins, Kume Island (宇江城城跡)

    Gusuku ruins on the 310 m summit of Uegusuku-dake — the highest castle site in Okinawa Prefecture — with a 360-degree view over almost the whole of Kume Island. Free. Designated a National Historic Site in 2009.

    Look for Okinawa's highest gusuku

    Uegusuku, Kumejima, Okinawa (summit of Uegusuku-dake)

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Kumejimakanko, Agency For Cultural Affairs

  3. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Kerama & nearby islands

    Wayama Mozuku, Zamami (和山海雲)

    A mozuku farmer's own restaurant three minutes' walk from Zamami port, serving soba made with thick mozuku grown in the Kerama sea; Okinawa Times praised the firm noodles' match with the seaweed's texture. It also sells its mozuku and runs snorkel tours.

    9 Zamami, Zamami Village, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Smartmagazine

  4. Must see · Kerama & nearby islands

    Furuzamami Beach, Zamami Island (古座間味ビーチ)

    Zamami's best beach, a 20-minute walk from the port: 'Kerama blue' water and reef straight off the sand; holds two Michelin Green Guide stars per the village.

    Look for Kerama-blue beach

    Zamami, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Japan-guide

  5. Must see · Kerama & nearby islands

    Aharen Beach, Tokashiki Island (阿波連ビーチ)

    Tokashiki's main beach in the Kerama Islands National Park: a long curve of white sand and 'Kerama blue' reef water, with a campground nearby.

    Look for Kerama beach

    Aharen, Tokashiki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  6. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Kerama & nearby islands

    Nantō Shokurakuen, Kume Island (南島食楽園)

    Big open izakaya by Eef Beach built around Kume's own produce: kuruma prawns raised in deep-ocean water, sea grapes, island red chicken, grouper and octopus, from Okinawan plates to nigiri.

    160-81 Higa, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  7. Must see · Teishoku, Curry & Yōshoku · Kerama & nearby islands

    Restaurant Marumi-ya, Zamami (レストラン まるみ屋)

    Five minutes from Zamami port: hearty daily set lunches built on island produce — mozuku seaweed champuru and house-made jīmāmi peanut tofu are the favourites.

    Zamami village, Zamami Island, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  8. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Kerama & nearby islands

    Kumejima Soba-dokoro Yan-kō, Kume Island (久米島そば処 やん小～)

    Soba shop in an old Ryūkyū-style house making hand-cut noodles with Kume's deep-sea water; the signature is a rare miso-flavoured soba piled with island-grown bean sprouts. Lunch only (11:30-13:30), closed Sundays.

    509 Nakadomari, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Kumejimakanko

  9. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Kerama & nearby islands

    Yukui-dokoro Washima, Kume Island (ゆくい処 笑島)

    Kume-jima's kuruma-prawn soba, built on an Okinawa-soba dashi with a paste of the island's farmed kuruma prawns and local miso, won the grand prix at the 'Nippon no Takaramono' world competition held in Singapore. The shop sells around 60 bowls a day and often sells out.

    1372-1 Nishime, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive

  10. Worth the detour · Kerama & nearby islands

    Tatami-ishi, Kume Island (畳石)

    About a thousand pentagonal and hexagonal andesite columns, each 1–1.5 m across, exposed at low tide on the south shore of Ōjima, bridged to Kume Island — a Miocene lava field that looks like tatami mats.

    Look for Columnar-jointed rock flat

    Ōjima, Kumejima, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Lonely Planet, Visit Okinawa

  11. Worth the detour · Kerama & nearby islands

    Inazaki Observatory, Zamami (稲崎展望台)

    Hilltop lookout on Zamami's north side, about an hour's walk from the port; on clear days Aguni, Tonaki and Kume islands are visible, and it is the best spot for watching humpback whales, which frequent these waters December–April. Part of Keramashotō National Park.

    Look for Whale-watching lookout

    Northern tip of Zamami Island, Zamami-son, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, JNTO — japan.travel food itineraries, Env NP

  12. Worth the detour · Kerama & nearby islands

    Gushikawa Castle Ruins, Kume Island (具志川城跡)

    Fifteenth-century gusuku on a cliff-bound headland in Kume Island's north-west, four low-walled enclosures above the East China Sea; National Historic Site since 1975.

    Look for Clifftop gusuku

    Nakamura, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Jcastle.info — Guide to Japanese Castles

  13. Worth the detour · Kerama & nearby islands

    Eef Beach, Kume Island (イーフビーチ)

    Two kilometres of white sand on Kume's east coast, one of Japan's '100 Best Beaches', facing the lagoon and Hate-no-hama.

    Look for Beach

    Higa, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Visit Okinawa

  14. Worth the detour · Kerama & nearby islands

    Ama Beach, Zamami Island (阿真ビーチ)

    The quieter of Zamami's two main beaches, on the southwest shore facing the uninhabited islets of Gahi and Agenashiku; sea turtles graze offshore.

    Look for Beach (sea turtles)

    Ama, Zamami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Visit Okinawa

  15. Worth the detour · Kerama & nearby islands

    Takatsukiyama Observatory, Zamami (高月山展望台)

    Hilltop lookout over Zamami village, Furuzamami Beach and the scattered Kerama islands — the classic Kerama Blue panorama.

    Look for Island viewpoint

    Zamami, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Fun! Japan (JTB)

  16. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Kerama & nearby islands

    Sukeroku Kamaboko, Kume Island (助ろく)

    Kume's fish-cake maker, carrying on a 60-year-old craft: chewy island kamaboko flavoured with kuruma prawn, mozuku or squid ink — a classic island snack.

    423-1 Kadekaru, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawa Times

  17. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Kerama & nearby islands

    Yonejima Shuzō awamori distillery, Kume Island (米島酒造)

    Small Kume Island distillery founded by Tabata Ryōtoku, who was drawn by the island's abundant water and varied geology; shop open 10-12 and 14-17, closed Sundays.

    499 Ōta, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Kumejimakanko, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  18. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Kerama & nearby islands

    Boku no Mise Ojisan, Zamami (ぼくの店 おじさん)

    A local favourite three minutes' walk from Zamami port, known for a hearty katsudon alongside soba and chanpurū lunch plates. It is listed on Zamami Village's official guide map.

    13 Zamami, Zamami Village, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), TV Tokyo — Cambria Palace (カンブリア宮殿)

  19. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Kerama & nearby islands

    Restaurant Namiji, Kume Island (レストラン波路)

    An island restaurant in Janadō that the Okinawa Times profiles for its spread of local seafood — Kume-jima's farmed kuruma-ebi prawns, mozuku seaweed, and ikasumi-jiru squid-ink soup — drawing both tourists and residents. The Kume-jima Tourism Association lists it among the island's eateries and notes the soups can be added to a lunch set cheaply.

    548-32 Janadō, Kumejima, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Kumejimakanko

Miyako Islands 40

Miyako-jima · Irabu · Ikema · Kurima

  1. Must see · Miyako Islands

    Tōri-ike, Shimoji Island (通り池)

    Two collapsed-cave sinkholes in the coral of Shimoji's west coast — 75 m and 55 m across, linked to each other and the sea by an underwater cave — the 'dragon's eyes', a national Natural Monument and a celebrated cave dive.

    Look for Twin sinkholes

    Sawada, Irabu, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Miyakojima City cultural-properties site, Visit Okinawa

  2. Must see · Miyako Islands

    Irabu Ōhashi Bridge (伊良部大橋)

    Opened 31 January 2015: at 3,540 m Japan's longest toll-free bridge, arcing over turquoise shallows from Miyako to Irabu Island.

    Look for Japan's longest free bridge

    Hirara–Irabu, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  3. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Miyako Islands

    Kojasobaya (古謝そば屋)

    Miyako soba shop founded in 1932 by the Koja noodle-making family, under a red-tile roof; lunchtime queues for Miyako soba, soki soba and curry soba.

    1517-1 Shimozato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawa Times

  4. Must see · Miyako Islands

    Yonaha Maehama Beach (与那覇前浜)

    Seven kilometres of white sand on Miyako's south-west tip, facing Kurima Island — the beach that usually tops rankings of Japan's best.

    Look for Japan's top-ranked beach

    Yonaha, Shimoji, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, JNTO — japan.travel food itineraries

  5. Must see · Miyako Islands

    Sunayama Beach (砂山ビーチ)

    Cove reached over a tall sand dune 4 km north of Hirara, framed by a natural rock arch — one of Miyako's signature beaches.

    Look for Dune-and-arch beach

    Nikadori, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  6. Must see · Miyako Islands

    Cape Higashi-hennazaki (東平安名崎)

    A 2 km finger of land at Miyako's south-east tip, strewn with tsunami boulders, ending at a 1967 white lighthouse with a 320° ocean panorama.

    Look for Cape & lighthouse

    1221-14 Bora, Gusukube, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Lonely Planet

  7. Must see · Miyako Islands

    17END, Shimoji Island (17エンド)

    The shallows off the end of Shimoji Airport's runway 17, where a sandbar appears at low tide in remarkably clear turquoise water — about 15–20 minutes' drive from Miyako over the Irabu Bridge.

    Look for Low-tide sandbar & lagoon

    Shimoji, Irabu, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  8. Must see · Miyako Islands

    Toguchi-no-hama Beach, Irabu Island (渡口の浜)

    An 800 m gently curving arc of fine white sand on south-west Irabu, renowned across Okinawa for its powdery sand and clear water, looking across to Miyako and Kurima islands; counted among Irabu's finest beaches.

    Look for Irabu's 800 m white-sand arc

    Irabu, Miyakojima, Okinawa (south-west Irabu Island)

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  9. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Miyako Islands

    Irabu Soba Kame (伊良部そば かめ)

    Irabu Island's soba stop, where the bonito hits you first; reached over the Irabu Bridge and named in both Okinawa Times' Miyako soba coverage and Mapple's Miyako-soba top ten.

    Irabu, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  10. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Miyako Islands

    Maruyoshi Shokudō (丸吉食堂)

    Out in Gusukube, a family shokudō serving the owner's mother's Miyako soba: pork-bone broth perfumed with garlic and big soki ribs.

    975 Sunagawa, Gusukube, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  11. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Miyako Islands

    Awamori to Okinawa Ryōri Gōya, Miyako (泡盛と沖縄料理 郷家)

    Hirara's classic shimauta izakaya: Miyako's own awamori brands, island home cooking, and nightly sanshin folk-song sets that end with the whole room dancing kachāshī.

    Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  12. Worth the detour · Miyako Islands

    Painagama Beach, Hirara (パイナガマビーチ)

    The closest beach to downtown Hirara, walkable from the port; its name (南長間) means 'long southern beach' in Miyako dialect. A barrier-free city beach popular for sunset and an easy first swim on Miyako.

    Look for Miyako's walk-in town beach, minutes from Hirara

    338-3 Shimozato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ocvb, Miyakokanko, Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Wikipedia JA

  13. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Miyako Islands

    Kikunotsuyu Shuzō awamori distillery, Miyako (菊之露酒造)

    Founded in 1928 in Hirara, Kikunotsuyu is one of Miyako's oldest and best-known awamori distillers, using the island's mineral-rich hard water from its coral-limestone bedrock; its aged awamori features in the Okinawa Regional Taxation Bureau's awamori appraisal.

    290 Nishizato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Tabirai, JSS, Nta, Wikipedia JA

  14. Worth the detour · Miyako Islands

    Ikema Island & Ikema Ōhashi (池間島)

    Fishing island off Miyako's northern tip, reached by the 1.4 km Ikema Ōhashi over shallow turquoise reef.

    Look for Bridge-linked island

    Ikema, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Lonely Planet, Visit Okinawa

  15. Worth the detour · Miyako Islands

    Miyako Jinja — Japan's southernmost shrine, Hirara (宮古神社)

    Founded in 1590 (Tenshō 18), Miyako Jinja is the southernmost Shinto shrine in Japan. It enshrines the three Kumano deities alongside three deified Miyako chieftains (tuyumya), including Nakasone Tuyumya; its annual festival falls on 26 October.

    Look for Japan's southernmost Shinto shrine, in central Hirara

    5-1 Nishizato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Tanoshima, Official Site

  16. Worth the detour · Miyako Islands

    Imgya Marine Garden, Gusukube (イムギャーマリンガーデン)

    A city-run seaside park built around a natural, wave-sheltered inlet (Imgya / Ingya coast) on Miyako's south shore, set up to promote marine recreation and tourism; the calm water suits snorkelling and a walking trail climbs to a lookout over the cove.

    Look for Calm natural inlet for snorkelling on Miyako's south coast

    605-2 Tomori, Gusukube, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Miyakokanko, Wikipedia JA, Tanoshima

  17. Worth the detour · Miyako Islands

    Cape Nishi-hennazaki, Karimata (西平安名崎)

    The cape at Miyako's north-western tip, facing the East China Sea, with a lookout over Ikema Ōhashi and Ikema Island. Its wind turbines were felled by typhoons in 2002–03 and three were rebuilt in 2008.

    Look for Wind-turbine cape with a panorama of Ikema Ōhashi

    Karimata, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Miyakokanko, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Wikipedia JA

  18. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Miyako Islands

    Okinohikari Shuzō awamori distillery, Miyako (沖之光酒造)

    Founded in 1948 (as Kosa Shuzō; Okinohikari since 1979), this Hirara distillery keeps about 70 % of its stock as aged kūsu; its 100 % ten-year-aged Okinohikari won the Okinawa Regional Taxation Bureau Director's Award at the 2005 awamori appraisal.

    1174 Shimozato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Tabirai, Jtajournal, JSS

  19. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Miyako Islands

    Cafe Uesuya, Miyako (カフェ ウエスヤ)

    A creative Asian café opened in 2014 on a Hirara back lane (in the owner's grandfather's former dental clinic) and since relocated within Shimozato, Hirara. At lunch it serves three original takes on Miyako soba; the signature 'Asian Miyako soba' is a pho-like bowl topped with coriander, nira and tomato.

    43 Shimozato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Okinawaclip

  20. Worth the detour · Miyako Islands

    Kurima Island & Kurima Ōhashi (来間島)

    Small island reached by the 1.7 km Kurima Ōhashi from Miyako's south-west, with café stops and Nagamahama beach looking back across to Maehama.

    Look for Bridge-linked island

    Kurima, Shimoji, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Visit Okinawa

  21. Worth the detour · Miyako Islands

    Aragusuku Beach, Miyako (新城海岸)

    East-coast reef beach where shallow, glass-clear water puts coral and tropical fish within a few strokes of the sand — Miyako's easy snorkel spot.

    Look for Snorkel beach

    Aragusuku, Gusukube, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Visit Okinawa

  22. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Miyako Islands

    Oshokujidokoro Sumubari, Karimata (お食事処 すむばり)

    A shokudō by the approach to Ikema Ōhashi that specialises in Miyako's little-known local octopus: its signature 'Sumubari soba' and an ink-black octopus soba use tako from the nearby fishing ports. Tabirai lists it among nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for; Smart Magazine explains how the kitchen makes the octopus so tender.

    768-4 Karimata, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Tabirai, Smartmagazine

  23. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Miyako Islands

    Kaimiru, Ikema Island (海美来)

    A pink-fronted seafood shokudō at the Ikema Island end of Ikema Ōhashi, looking out over 'Ikema blue'. Its turban-shell sazae soba is found nowhere else, per Tabirai's list of nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for; the Miyako island tourism association also lists its handmade purple-sweet-potato mochi.

    〒906-0421 1173-7 Ikema, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Tabirai, Tanoshima

  24. Worth the detour · Tofu, Shōjin & Vegetarian · Miyako Islands

    Shima Tōfu Haru-obaa Shokudō, Miyako (島とうふ 春おばぁ食堂)

    A shokudō built around a family island-tofu business of more than 60 years; its most popular dish is yushi-dōfu soba, Miyako soba crowned with soft freshly-set tofu. Tabirai includes it in its nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for, and Mapple lists it among Miyako's top-ten Miyako soba lunches.

    3107-140 Shimozato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Tabirai, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  25. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Miyako Islands

    Rakuen no Kajitsu, Kurima Island (楽園の果実)

    Farm café on Kurima Island using its own tree-ripened mango (July–Aug) and dragon fruit (July–Oct) in parfaits and sweets, plus a Miyako-beef rice bowl.

    476-1 Kurima, Shimoji, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  26. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Miyako Islands

    Doug's Burger Miyakojima (ダグズ・バーガー)

    Island burger joint using 100 % Miyako-island beef, plus a burger of local yellow-fin tuna — the Miyako take on Okinawa's American-era burger culture.

    1153-3-101 Shimozato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Visit Okinawa, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  27. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Miyako Islands

    Inaka Ryōri no Mise Kura, Miyako (田舎料理の店 蔵)

    Country-cooking izakaya in Hirara using island miso in champuru and rafute; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine and a Mapple guidebook pick.

    654-6 Hisagai, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Prefecture — 「琉球料理が味わえる店」 certification, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  28. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Miyako Islands

    Yamato Shokudō (大和食堂)

    Hirara regulars' shop serving the same plain, honest Miyako soba for some forty years.

    819-3 Nishizato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  29. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Miyako Islands

    Minato Shokudō, Miyako (みなと食堂)

    Harbour-side shokudō near Sunayama whose house noodles are kneaded with aosa seaweed and served in a broth from bonito trimmings — a taste found only here.

    593-10 Nikadori, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  30. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Miyako Islands

    Jinku-ya (じんく屋)

    Counter run by Kusamatsu Seimen, one of Miyako's two big noodle makers: chewy fresh noodles, simple bonito soup.

    84 Shimozato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  31. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Miyako Islands

    RICCO gelato, Miyako (リッコジェラート)

    Italian-trained gelato maker in Hirara churning Miyako's own mangoes, fruits and even island salt and vegetables into some thirty flavours.

    550 Shimozato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  32. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Miyako Islands

    Shima Café Tunkaraya, Miyako (島cafe とぅんからや)

    Hilltop café in southern Miyako looking over the sea, cooking 'made in Miyako' lunches and fruit-heavy desserts.

    1214 Shinzato, Ueno, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  33. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Miyako Islands

    Yukishio Museum, Miyako (雪塩ミュージアム)

    Showroom of the 'Yukishio' salt works, which makes powder-fine salt from limestone-filtered underground seawater; free guided looks at the production line, and the shop's Yukishio soft-serve is the draw.

    191 Karimata, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  34. Worth the detour · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Miyako Islands

    Sakana-dokoro Shiken-bara, Miyako (肴処 志堅原)

    Constantly-full izakaya on Hirara's Nishizato-dōri izakaya strip, serving fresh fish from the waters around Miyako as sashimi and salt-simmered mās-ni, with island awamori.

    236 Nishizato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  35. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Miyako Islands

    Blue Turtle, Irabu Island (ブルー タートル)

    White sea-view café-restaurant on Irabu Island right in front of Toguchi-no-hama, one of Irabu's finest beaches; known for hamburg steak and for ice cream served over hidden layers of coloured shaved ice.

    Irabu, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan (facing Toguchi-no-hama beach)

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  36. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Miyako Islands

    Okinawa Soba Marukami, Miyako (沖縄そば まるかみ)

    A soba shop in the Kurima settlement on Kurima Island, run by a former hotel-restaurant cook. The house Marukami soba comes with homemade fresh noodles and bonito broth, topped with seasoned pork belly, tender cartilage sōki and a thin egg crepe. A plain su-soba is also on the menu. Lunch only, 11:00–14:30.

    91 Kurima (下地来間), Shimoji, Kurima Island, Miyakojima-shi, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  37. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Miyako Islands

    Ikemajima gelato cafe Ninufa, Ikema Island (ニヌファ)

    An Italian-style gelato café on Ikema Island whose name means 'North Star' in Miyako dialect; every seat on its coral-rock terrace faces the sea. Gelato is made without artificial flavouring, colouring or preservatives in local flavours, with wood-fired pizza alongside.

    976-1 Maezato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa 906-0422, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Cotrip

  38. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Miyako Islands

    Koshibaru Shokudō, Miyako (腰原食堂)

    A Hirara soba shokudō whose house creation is the spicy 'dragon soba', made by adding Chinese-style chicken stock to the bonito-and-pork Miyako soba broth; it also serves a plain Miyako soba. Mapple lists it among Miyako's ten most popular Miyako soba lunch spots.

    1325-3 Shimozato, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Smartmagazine

  39. Deep cut · Miyako Islands

    Ikema Wetlands, Ikema Island (池間湿原)

    At 38 ha the largest wetland in Okinawa Prefecture, in the centre of Ikema Island; selected as one of Japan's 500 Important Wetlands, and since 1 Nov 2011 the whole island is a national wildlife (bird) protection area. An observation tower overlooks the marsh and its migratory birds.

    Look for Okinawa's largest wetland, a birding stop on Ikema

    Ikema, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Tanoshima, Midorihana

  40. Deep cut · Miyako Islands

    Mamoru-kun police-officer figures, Miyako (宮古島まもる君)

    Life-size painted policeman figures posted at Miyako crossings by the traffic-safety association since the 1990s — now the island's cult mascot.

    Look for Quirky roadside figures

    Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

Yaeyama Islands 48

Ishigaki · Iriomote · Taketomi · Hateruma · Yonaguni

  1. Must see · Yaeyama Islands

    Taketomi Island & village (竹富島)

    Fifteen minutes by ferry from Ishigaki: a preserved Ryūkyū village of coral-stone walls, red-tiled houses and white-sand lanes travelled by water-buffalo cart — a national Important Preservation District since 1987 — ringed by Kondoi Beach.

    Look for Preserved Ryūkyū village island

    Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Lonely Planet

  2. Must see · Yaeyama Islands

    Hoshizuna-no-hama star sand beach, Iriomote (星砂の浜)

    Small north-shore Iriomote beach whose 'sand' includes millions of star-shaped foraminifera skeletons; snorkelling over the reef straight off the beach.

    Look for Star-sand beach

    Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Japan-guide

  3. Must see · Yaeyama Islands

    Pinaisara Falls, Iriomote (ピナイサーラの滝)

    Okinawa Prefecture's highest waterfall — a 54 m drop on the Hinai River, reached by kayaking the Hinai mangroves and a jungle trail inside Iriomote-Ishigaki National Park.

    Look for Okinawa's tallest waterfall

    Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa (Iriomote Island)

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Lonely Planet, Env NP

  4. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Yaeyama Islands

    Shima Ryōri Izakaya Adan-tei, Ishigaki (島料理居酒屋 あだん亭)

    Ishigaki town izakaya cooking genuinely Yaeyaman dishes from island produce — try the champuru of adan (screw-pine) shoots — and the only Yaeyama restaurant on the prefecture's Ryukyu-cuisine certified list.

    East 1F, 430 Ōkawa, Ishigaki, Okinawa 907-0022, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Prefecture — 「琉球料理が味わえる店」 certification, Okinawatraveler, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  5. Must see · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Yaeyama Islands

    Seifuku Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (請福酒造)

    Ishigaki awamori maker founded in 1949, with a direct shop where the whole Seifuku range can be tasted and free ~15-minute factory tours at set times, no booking needed.

    959 Miyara, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Yaeyamavb, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報)

  6. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Yaeyama Islands

    Pengin Shokudō, Ishigaki (辺銀食堂)

    Birthplace of Ishigaki-jima rāyu, the hand-made island-salt-and-chilli oil that started Japan's 'edible rāyu' boom; at lunch the house order is jājan-suba (thick noodles with spicy miso), served until sold out.

    Ishigaki city centre (7 min walk from Ishigaki bus terminal), Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Gigazine, macaroni (macaro-ni.jp)

  7. Must see · Yaeyama Islands

    Kabira Bay (川平湾)

    Turquoise-to-emerald bay on Ishigaki's north coast, a national Place of Scenic Beauty inside Iriomote-Ishigaki National Park; swimming is banned, so see it by glass-bottom boat over the black-pearl farms.

    Look for Scenic bay

    Kabira, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  8. Must see · Yaeyama Islands

    Iriomote Island jungle & mangroves (西表島)

    Okinawa's second-largest island, about 90 % jungle and mangrove — part of the 2021 UNESCO natural World Heritage site and home of the critically endangered Iriomote cat; explored by river cruise and kayak (Urauchi River, Pinaisara Falls — the prefecture's tallest at 55 m).

    Look for UNESCO jungle island

    Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  9. Must see · Yaeyama Islands

    Cape Irizaki, Yonaguni — Japan's westernmost point (西崎)

    Cliff-ringed cape at the west tip of Yonaguni, the last place in Japan to see the sunset: lighthouse, lookout and the 'westernmost point of Japan' monument; Taiwan, 107 km away, is visible on clear days.

    Look for Japan's westernmost point

    Yonaguni, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Visit Okinawa

  10. Must see · Yaeyama Islands

    Nishihama Beach, Hateruma Island (ニシ浜)

    The beach that gave its name to 'Hateruma Blue' — powder-white sand and impossibly saturated turquoise water on Japan's southernmost inhabited island; stay overnight for the star-field sky.

    Look for Beach ('Hateruma Blue')

    Hateruma, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  11. Must see · Yaeyama Islands

    Takanazaki & Japan's Southernmost Point Monument, Hateruma (高那崎・日本最南端の碑)

    Kilometre-long limestone cliffs at the southern tip of Hateruma, Japan's southernmost inhabited island, where a monument to the southernmost point (erected 1970) stands beside Taketomi Town's peace monument and a path of stones from every prefecture.

    Look for Japan's southernmost inhabited point

    Hateruma Island, Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa (south tip; ~10 min by car from Hateruma port)

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Taketomikanko

  12. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Yaeyama Islands

    Kinatsuyu (八重山そば処 来夏世)

    Old-house Yaeyama-soba specialist in Ishigaki town keeping the simple, light traditional flavour; the soba set with jūshī rice draws a noon queue. 'The royal road of Yaeyama soba' in the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll.

    203 Ishigaki, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  13. Must see · Wagyu, Yakiniku & Sukiyaki · Yaeyama Islands

    Ishigaki-gyū Sumibi Yakiniku Yamamoto (石垣牛 炭火焼肉 やまもと)

    The Ishigaki-beef yakiniku house locals queue for: buying whole animals means rare cuts on the board, grilled over charcoal; opens at 17:00 and closes when the meat runs out.

    2-5-18 Hamasaki-chō, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  14. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Yaeyama Islands

    Sobadokoro Takenoko, Taketomi (そば処 竹の子)

    Taketomi's most popular eating house, around forty years old, ladling the previous generation's Yaeyama soba in the red-tile village.

    Taketomi Village, Taketomi Island, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  15. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Yaeyama Islands

    Maguro Senmon Izakaya Hitoshi, Ishigantō (まぐろ専門居酒屋 ひとし 石敢當店)

    Ishigaki's famous tuna izakaya, packed with locals and visitors alike for heaped plates of just-landed island tuna; book or queue at 16:30.

    197-1 Ōkawa, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  16. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Yaeyama Islands

    KITCHEN inaba, Iriomote (キッチン イナバ)

    Iriomote's island-food kitchen near Uehara port: rare local ingredients — irabu sea-snake soup, gazami crab, Ryukyu wild boar in season — alongside traditional and Western-style plates, with jungle-green mountains in the windows.

    742-6 Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  17. Must see · Wagyu, Yakiniku & Sukiyaki · Yaeyama Islands

    Yakiniku Takesan-tei, Ishigaki (焼肉 たけさん亭)

    Ishigaki-beef yakiniku whose owner holds cattle-auction buying rights and buys whole A4–A5 animals, so rarer cuts appear on the menu. Dinner only (closed Tue).

    2-2-4 Hamasaki-chō, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Yaeyamavb

  18. Must see · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Yaeyama Islands

    Sakimoto Shuzōsho — hanazake distillery, Yonaguni (崎元酒造所)

    Yonaguni's oldest distillery, still firing a traditional direct-fire pot still by hand; maker of the awamori 'Yonaguni' and of hanazake, the 60% first-run spirit that only Yonaguni is permitted to make. Distillery shop sells brewery-only bottles.

  19. Must see · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Yaeyama Islands

    Akashi Shokudō, Ishigaki (明石食堂)

    Old-guard north-Ishigaki shokudō about 40 minutes' drive from town, with queues before opening for its soft-bone sōki Yaeyama soba — clean pork-bone broth over round straight noodles. Ranked No.1 in a 2019 Okinawa-soba ranking reported by Ryukyu Shimpo.

    Recommended by Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報)

  20. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Yaeyama Islands

    Taira Shōten, Ishigaki (平良商店)

    A Tonoshiro soba shop facing Manta Park that won the grand prix of the Yaeyama-soba division at the 3rd Yaeyama Soba Championship (2017). Tabirai describes it as a locals' favourite for its soft-cartilage sōki soba and spicy miso vegetable soba, made with a broth from island moromi-pork bones; the Okinawa Times reported FamilyMart selling a cup-noodle version supervised by the shop.

    506 Tonoshiro, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Tabirai, Okinawa Times, Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks), Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive

  21. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Yaeyama Islands

    Café Tēdun Shidamē-kan, Taketomi Island (カフェ てぇーどぅん しだめー館)

    A red-tiled café beneath the Nagomi-no-tō lookout in Taketomi village, about 12 minutes' walk from the port. It was one of the winners at the first Yaeyama Soba Championship in 2015, the year Komatsu took the Yaeyama-soba grand prix.

    361 Aza-Taketomi, Taketomi-chō, Yaeyama-gun, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Ishigakikeizai, Taketomikanko, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  22. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Tōrin-ji & Gongen-dō, Ishigaki (桃林寺・権現堂)

    Gongen-dō, beside Tōrin-ji temple in central Ishigaki, was first built in 1614, destroyed by the great Meiwa tsunami of 1771 and rebuilt; it was designated a national Important Cultural Property in 1981. The Agency for Cultural Affairs' database notes decorative details unusual in mainland shrine architecture and calls it Japan's southernmost surviving early-modern religious building of this scale.

    Look for Japan's southernmost Important Cultural Property shrine hall, rebuilt after the 1771 tsunami

    285 Ishigaki, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Agency For Cultural Affairs, Ishigakicity, Yaeyamavb

  23. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Yubu Island water-buffalo crossing (由布島)

    Tiny island off Iriomote reached by water-buffalo cart across a shallow sandy strait, often to a sanshin song from the driver; a botanical garden and cafés on the island.

    Look for Buffalo-cart island

    Komi, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa, JNTO — japan.travel food itineraries

  24. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Urauchi River & Mariyudu Falls, Iriomote (浦内川・マリユドゥの滝)

    Okinawa's longest river: a boat cruise up the mangrove-lined Urauchi, then a jungle walk to Mariyudu Falls, a two-tier fall selected among Japan's 100 best waterfalls.

    Look for River cruise to a top-100 waterfall

    Urauchi, Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa (Iriomote Island)

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Wikivoyage, Env NP

  25. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Nishi-sanbashi West Pier, Taketomi Island (西桟橋)

    A 105 m limestone-and-concrete pier built in 1938 on Taketomi's west coast. Islanders once sailed from here to farm rice paddies on Iriomote. It went out of use around 1971 and was registered as a Tangible Cultural Property in 2005. It is now the island's sunset spot, and it is the key-visual location of the film 'Non Non Biyori Vacation', which the Anime Tourism Association listed in its '88 Anime Pilgrimage Sites' from 2019 to 2024.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Non Non Biyori Vacation (2018 film) — the West Pier is the film's key visual; Anime Tourism 88 Yaeyama/Taketomi entry 2019–2024 · Sunset pier and Non Non Biyori key visual

    207 Taketomi, Taketomi Town, Yaeyama District, Okinawa 907-1101, Japan

    Recommended by ANIMETOURISM88, Agency For Cultural Affairs, Taketomikanko

  26. Worth the detour · Sake, Awamori, Whisky & Bars · Yaeyama Islands

    Yaesen Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (八重泉酒造)

    Founded in 1955; the factory shop shows a 15-minute film of the distilling process and runs a tasting counter with shop-only bottles. Three Yaesen awamori won awards at a UK spirits competition (Ryukyu Shimpo).

    1834 Ishigaki, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Yaeyamavb, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報)

  27. Worth the detour · Tofu, Shōjin & Vegetarian · Yaeyama Islands

    Tōfu no Higa, Ishigaki (とうふの比嘉)

    A family tofu maker of more than 70 years, now run by the third generation, that opens at 6:30 am and sells out before noon. It is known for yushi-dōfu, tofu ladled out before it sets. The Kariyushi set adds egg, rice or porridge, okara and soy milk. Closed Sundays.

    570 Ishigaki, Ishigaki-shi, Okinawa 907-0023, Japan

    Recommended by Okinawa Television (otv) — Okitive, Ryukyu Shimpo (琉球新報), Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  28. Worth the detour · Markets, Depachika & Street Food · Yaeyama Islands

    Ishigaki City Public Market (石垣市公設市場)

    Ishigaki's 'kitchen' since 1899 (on this site since 1904), a three-storey public market in the Euglena Mall arcade: local produce and fish at street level, the Ishigaki City specialty-products centre above and a shokudō on top; an eat-in space was added in the May 2021 renewal.

    208 Ōkawa, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan (Euglena Mall)

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com), Wikipedia JA

  29. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Mount Omoto (於茂登岳)

    At 525.5 m the highest peak in Okinawa Prefecture, rising from the Omoto range on Ishigaki's north; a forest trail climbs to views over Kabira and the reef. Paired with Kabira Bay as a national Place of Scenic Beauty.

    Look for Okinawa's highest peak

    Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Wikipedia

  30. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Miyara Dunchi (宮良殿内)

    Residence of a Ryūkyū-kingdom official built in 1819 in the style of Shuri samurai houses — an Important Cultural Property with a rock garden that is a Place of Scenic Beauty; still lived in, so viewed from outside.

    Look for 1819 official's residence

    Ōkawa, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Wikipedia

  31. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Yonekoyaki Shisa Park, Ishigaki (米子焼工房 シーサー園)

    Roadside garden behind the Yonekoyaki pottery workshop crowded with giant, psychedelic, pop-art shisa lion-dog sculptures.

    Look for Outsider-art shisa garden

    447-1 Fukai, Ishigaki, Okinawa 907-0451, Japan

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  32. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Tamatorizaki Observation Point, Ishigaki (玉取崎展望台)

    Hilltop platform on Ishigaki's east coast looking over Cape Tamatori, Ibaruma Bay, the hilly Hirakubo peninsula and the reef.

    Look for Viewpoint

    Ibaruma, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  33. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Ishigaki Yaima Village (石垣やいま村)

    Open-air village of century-old Yaeyama houses (designated tangible cultural properties) beside a mangrove, with folk-song shows, crafts and the Anparu Shokudō serving Okinawa soba and jūshī.

    Look for Open-air folk village

    Nagura, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Stars and Stripes Okinawa, Visit Okinawa

  34. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Yonaguni Monument underwater formation (与那国島海底地形)

    Terraced underwater rock formation found by a diver in 1986 off Yonaguni's south coast — natural or man-made is still debated; reached on dive and glass-bottom boat trips.

    Look for Underwater 'ruins' dive

    off Arakawabana, Yonaguni, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Stars and Stripes Okinawa

  35. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Ishigaki-jima Limestone Cave (石垣島鍾乳洞)

    Japan's southernmost show cave: 3.2 km of limestone formed over some 200,000 years in southern Ishigaki, with a lit walkway through the formations.

    Look for Show cave

    Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  36. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Cape Hirakubo & lighthouse, Ishigaki (平久保崎)

    The northern tip of Ishigaki's Hirakubo Peninsula; from the white lighthouse the Pacific lies on one side and the East China Sea on the other.

    Look for Ishigaki's northern tip

    Hirakubo, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia JA, Yaeyamavb

  37. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Cape Agarizaki, Yonaguni (東崎)

    Cliff-top cape at Yonaguni's eastern end, grazed by Yonaguni horses, with views across to Iriomote on clear days.

    Look for Eastern cliffs & Yonaguni horses

    Agarizaki, Yonaguni, Yaeyama, Okinawa, Japan

  38. Worth the detour · Yaeyama Islands

    Kondoi Beach, Taketomi Island (コンドイ浜)

    Taketomi's west-coast swimming beach: white sand and a long, shallow emerald lagoon calm enough for small children; reached by rental bicycle from the village.

    Look for Shallow lagoon beach

    Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa, Japan

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing), Mapple (まっぷる, Shobunsha guidebooks)

  39. Worth the detour · Okinawan & Ryūkyū · Yaeyama Islands

    Kimi Shokudō, Ishigaki (キミ食堂)

    Ishigaki town shokudō famous for its miso-broth take on Yaeyama soba — a noodle-lovers' poll pick and one of Rurubu's 'creative' soba bowls.

    Recommended by Okinawa Times, Rurubu (るるぶ&more, JTB Publishing)

  40. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Yaeyama Islands

    Ishigaki-jima Milmil Honpo (石垣島ミルミル本舗)

    Mori no Kenja, Ishigaki (森の賢者)

    Small Ishigaki-town kitchen cooking island vegetables, fish and Ishigaki beef without chemical seasonings, with awamori, sake and more than 45 home-made fruit and herb liqueurs; book ahead.

    Shima Gourmet ROCO, Iriomote (島ぐるめ ROCO)

    Uehara dining room cooking Iriomote's sea and mountain catch — grilled crab, sashimi salad, squid-ink rice croquettes and grouper simmered in island salt.

    Takamine Shuzōsho awamori distillery, Kabira (高嶺酒造所)

    Small distillery beside Kabira Park making 'Omoto' awamori by hand — one of the few still using direct-fire (jika-bi) distillation; the process is visible through glass and tastings are offered.

    Yakiniku Kingyū, Ishigaki (焼肉 金牛)

    Run by an Ishigaki family that has raised wagyu on the island for over 120 years; serves only its own Ishigaki beef, raised ~30 months and aged. Dinner only (closed Thu).

    Fruit parlour popular with both locals and visitors on Ishigaki, with a long line-up of chilled sweets built on tropical island fruit; featured in its own Rurubu piece and in Mapple's Ishigaki sweets round-up.

  46. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Yaeyama Islands

    How Tree Gelato, Ishigaki (ハウトゥリージェラート)

    Specialist in cold-plate marble ice cream mixing fresh fruit from the owners' own farm with Ishigaki Island milk; seasonal (Feb-Nov).

    A Yaeyama-soba specialist named for its address, 'Aza-Ishigaki No. 1', a short walk from Ishigaki port's remote-island terminal (it also has a Naha branch). Tabirai's list of ten must-eat Yaeyama soba shops on Ishigaki includes it, and Rurubu features it.

    Ikehara Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (池原酒造)

191 sights and 234 places to eat across Okinawa — the Ryūkyū Kingdom’s castles and sacred groves, Okinawa soba counters and taco-rice joints, from Naha out to the Miyako and Yaeyama islands — every one traceable to its source.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a label alone doesn’t qualify. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it serves. Tabelog and Retty scores may measure popularity but never count as a source.

Web-searched in Japanese and English, fact-checked

Every place is traceable to two credible sources, or a lone UNESCO / Agency for Cultural Affairs designation — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor/Tabelog never count toward the two-source bar.

cleo
